title: Strictly correlated electrons in a quantum ring: from Kohn-Sham to Kantorovich potentials
summary: Our goal in this paper is twofold. First, we characterize the class of pairwise interactions for which the Seidl conjecture on the structure of optimal plans for the symmetric multimarginal optimal transport problem with one-dimensional marginal holds. This extends previous results by Colombo, De Pascale, and Di Marino [Can. Jou. Math., 67 (2015), https://doi.org/10.4153/CJM-2014-011-x], which treated the case of translation-invariant, convex and decreasing interactions. In particular, our results apply to physically relevant interactions for electrons living on a quantum ring. The second main goal of the paper is to rigorously derive the leading order asymptotics of the adiabatic connection potential for strongly interacting systems. More precisely, we show that for electrons in a quantum ring (or one-dimensional interval), not only the Lieb density functional converges to the optimal transport (or strictly correlated) functional in the semiclassical limit, but also the representing potential converges to a regular Kantorovich potential. As an intermediate step, we also extend previous results on the strongly interacting limit of the Lieb functional to periodic systems in arbitrary dimensions.

AI.tldr: This paper characterizes pairwise interactions validating the Seidl conjecture for symmetric multimarginal optimal transport in 1D, extending prior results to physically relevant quantum-ring electron interactions; it also rigorously derives leading-order asymptotics of the adiabatic connection potential in the strongly interacting limit, proving convergence of both the Lieb functional and its representing potential to the optimal transport (strictly correlated) functional and a regular Kantorovich potential, respectively—including extensions to periodic systems in arbitrary dimensions.
AI.motivation: To extend the validity of the Seidl conjecture to broader classes of pairwise interactions—especially those relevant to quantum many-body physics (e.g., electrons on a quantum ring)—and to rigorously establish the semiclassical and strongly interacting asymptotics of density functional theory quantities, specifically the adiabatic connection potential and Lieb functional.
AI.method: Mathematical analysis combining optimal transport theory, convex analysis, and quantum mechanical modeling; includes characterization of interaction kernels preserving cyclical monotonicity and optimality structure, asymptotic analysis of the Lieb functional in the strong-coupling limit, and derivation of Kantorovich potentials via duality and regularization techniques; extends prior work to non-translation-invariant and periodic settings.
AI.result: 1. Full characterization of pairwise interaction classes satisfying the Seidl conjecture for symmetric multimarginal OT with 1D marginals, including quantum-ring Coulomb-like interactions; 2. Rigorous proof that the Lieb functional converges to the strictly correlated (optimal transport) functional in the strong-interaction limit, even for periodic systems in arbitrary dimensions; 3. Convergence of the representing adiabatic connection potential to a regular (Lipschitz, differentiable a.e.) Kantorovich potential for 1D quantum rings and intervals.
AI.conclusion: The Seidl conjecture holds under significantly broader interaction assumptions than previously known, enabling rigorous DFT foundations for strongly correlated quantum systems; moreover, the adiabatic connection formalism is mathematically well-defined in the strong-coupling limit via optimal transport, with the potential acquiring regularity essential for practical approximations.

title: Dual contractions and algebraic families
summary: We introduce a duality for Inönü-Wigner contractions attached to real symmetric Lie algebras. Starting from a symmetric pair $(\mathfrak{g},θ)$, we define a dual real form $\mathfrak{g}^{*}$ inside the complexification of $\mathfrak{g}$ and consider the corresponding contraction with respect to the common fixed-point subalgebra $\mathfrak{g}^θ$. The main result shows that the original contraction and its dual appear as real fibers of a single algebraic family of complex Lie algebras equipped with an anti-holomorphic involution. This places the two contractions in one geometric framework and connects them with the algebraic-family methods developed in recent work on contractions, real forms, and hidden symmetries.

AI.tldr: Introduces a duality for Inönü-Wigner contractions of real symmetric Lie algebras via a dual real form and embeds both original and dual contractions as real fibers of a complex algebraic family with anti-holomorphic involution.
AI.motivation: To unify and geometrically interpret Inönü-Wigner contractions of real symmetric Lie algebras using duality and algebraic-family methods, linking them to recent developments in contractions, real forms, and hidden symmetries.
AI.method: Constructs a dual real form $\mathfrak{g}^{*}$ inside the complexification of $\mathfrak{g}$ from a symmetric pair $(\mathfrak{g}, \theta)$, defines contraction relative to the fixed-point subalgebra $\mathfrak{g}^\theta$, and embeds both original and dual contractions as real fibers of a complex algebraic family equipped with an anti-holomorphic involution.
AI.result: The original and dual Inönü-Wigner contractions are realized as real fibers of a single algebraic family of complex Lie algebras with anti-holomorphic involution, establishing a unified geometric framework.
AI.conclusion: This duality provides a coherent geometric and algebraic perspective on contractions of symmetric Lie algebras, integrating them into the broader context of algebraic families and real structures.

title: A second order upper bound to the free energy of the two dimensional Bose gas
summary: We consider a two-dimensional Bose gas in the dilute regime where $ρa^2$ is small. For temperatures below the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless critical temperature, we derive an explicit upper bound for the free energy density using Bogoliubov theory. Our result captures the contribution of quasiparticle modes with dispersion relation $\sqrt{p^4 + 8πρ\, δ\, p^2}$ and where $δ= 2 / (|\log(ρa^2)| + \log |\log(ρa^2)|)$.

AI.tldr: Derives an explicit upper bound for the free energy density of a 2D dilute Bose gas below the BKT transition temperature using Bogoliubov theory, incorporating a logarithmically corrected quasiparticle dispersion.
AI.motivation: To rigorously estimate the free energy density of a two-dimensional dilute Bose gas in the superfluid (BKT) phase, where standard mean-field approaches fail due to strong fluctuations.
AI.method: Applies Bogoliubov theory adapted to the 2D dilute regime; constructs trial states encoding quasiparticle excitations with a derived dispersion relation involving logarithmic corrections from interaction scaling.
AI.result: Obtains an explicit upper bound on the free energy density that accounts for the anomalous dispersion $\sqrt{p^4 + 8\pi\rho\, \delta\, p^2}$, with $\delta = 2 / (|\log(\rho a^2)| + \log |\log(\rho a^2)|)$, reflecting renormalized interaction effects.
AI.conclusion: Confirms that Bogoliubov theory—when suitably regularized with the correct logarithmic scaling—yields a quantitatively accurate upper bound for the free energy in the 2D BKT phase, bridging microscopic interaction parameters and macroscopic thermodynamics.

title: Higher (gauged) Wess--Zumino--Witten terms based on Lie crossed modules
summary: We derive higher Wess--Zumino--Witten (WZW) and gauged WZW (gWZW) terms within strict higher Chern--Simons (CS) gauge theory. Starting from the Cartan homotopy formula, we obtain the $(2n+2)$-dimensional higher CS forms and transgression forms for strict Lie 2-groups presented by Lie crossed modules. Given two 2-connections related by a higher gauge transformation, higher transgression forms yield canonical higher WZW and gWZW terms. We prove that, for the symmetric invariant polynomial associated with differential crossed modules, the pure-gauge higher WZW term vanishes identically, whereas the higher gWZW term is exact. Consequently, the higher CS action is higher-gauge invariant on closed manifolds, and on manifolds with boundary all gauge dependence is encoded in boundary terms.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs higher-dimensional WZW and gauged WZW terms from strict higher Chern–Simons theory using Lie 2-groups and crossed modules; it proves gauge invariance of the CS action, with all anomaly-like dependence confined to boundaries.
AI.motivation: To systematically derive higher Wess–Zumino–Witten and gauged WZW terms within a rigorous higher gauge-theoretic framework—specifically strict Lie 2-group Chern–Simons theory—and clarify their gauge behavior and boundary contributions.
AI.method: Uses the Cartan homotopy formula to construct (2n+2)-dimensional higher Chern–Simons and transgression forms for strict Lie 2-groups modeled by Lie crossed modules; derives higher WZW/gWZW terms as boundary contributions from higher gauge transformations; employs symmetric invariant polynomials on differential crossed modules to analyze exactness and vanishing properties.
AI.result: Higher pure-gauge WZW terms vanish identically; higher gauged WZW terms are exact; the higher CS action is fully higher-gauge invariant on closed manifolds, and on manifolds with boundary, gauge dependence resides solely in boundary terms.
AI.conclusion: The higher CS action admits a consistent, geometrically grounded definition of higher WZW and gWZW terms, ensuring gauge invariance up to boundary contributions—establishing a robust foundation for higher-dimensional sigma models and anomaly cancellation in extended field theories.

title: Understanding the structure of nucleon excitations from their wavefunctions
summary: Relativistic wavefunctions of nucleon excitations are scrutinised to understand their node structure and the underlying role of local interpolating fields in generating the nucleon spectrum. In addressing quark model perspectives, approximately 4000 propagators are employed on the heaviest PACS-CS ensemble at $m_π\simeq$ 702 MeV. We examine the ground and four lowest-lying excited states at zero momentum for both positive- and negative-parity spectra, where the proton's d-quark wavefunction is calculated about the two u quarks at the origin. This is achieved using two local interpolating fields that each carry the quantum numbers of the nucleon but with differing spin-flavour structures, one of which vanishes in the nonrelativistic limit. We find that two distinct types of wavefunction nodes are manifest: "superposition nodes" formed through a linear combination of interpolating fields, and novel "built-in nodes" that are fundamentally built in to the s-wave Dirac components of an individual interpolating field. These are investigated qualitatively through visualisations in the form of both volume and surface renderings, and quantitatively by the calculation of radial wavefunctions. Combined, these findings build a comprehensive picture of the single-particle nucleon spectrum and how its properties derive from fundamental lattice operators.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates nucleon excitation wavefunctions in lattice QCD using relativistic Dirac structure and local interpolating fields, identifying two types of nodes—'superposition' and 'built-in'—and linking them to spin-flavour operator structure and s-wave Dirac components.
AI.motivation: To understand the node structure of relativistic nucleon wavefunctions and clarify how local interpolating fields with distinct spin-flavour quantum numbers generate the observed nucleon spectrum, especially in relation to quark model expectations and the nonrelativistic limit.
AI.method: Lattice QCD analysis on the PACS-CS ensemble (m_π ≈ 702 MeV); computation of ~4000 quark propagators; extraction of ground and four lowest excited states (both parities) at zero momentum; use of two local nucleon-interpolating fields differing in spin-flavour structure—one vanishing in the nonrelativistic limit; visualisation (volume/surface renderings) and quantitative radial wavefunction analysis of d-quark wavefunctions relative to u-quark origin.
AI.result: Identification and characterisation of two node types: (i) 'superposition nodes', arising from linear combinations of interpolating fields, and (ii) 'built-in nodes', intrinsically present in s-wave Dirac components of individual fields; both types are confirmed qualitatively via 3D visualisations and quantitatively via radial profiles.
AI.conclusion: The nucleon excitation spectrum arises not only from superpositions of operators but also from intrinsic relativistic (Dirac) structure encoded in single interpolating fields—highlighting the essential role of local operator design and relativistic kinematics in lattice spectroscopy.

title: Visible Neutrino Decay As An Open Quantum System
summary: Decays of heavier neutrino mass eigenstates into lighter ones, while very slow in the Standard Model, can be significantly enhanced in scenarios with more than three neutrino flavours, or in models with new ultra-light particles such as Majorons. A full theoretical description is challenging due to the intricate interplay between oscillations and decay, interference between different decay channels, and the possibility of multi-step decay cascades. In this paper, we develop a fully general description of arbitrarily complex systems of oscillating and decaying neutrinos using methods from the theory of open quantum systems. Notably, we demonstrate how such systems can be implemented using the Lindblad master equation, the Liouvillian superoperator, as well as Kraus operators. The last two methods eschew the need for solving a differential equation, thereby showing superior numerical performance.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a general open quantum systems framework—using the Lindblad master equation, Liouvillian superoperator, and Kraus operators—to model oscillating and decaying neutrinos in multi-flavor or Majoron-coupled scenarios; Kraus and Liouvillian methods offer superior numerical efficiency over differential-equation-based approaches.
AI.motivation: Standard Model neutrino decays are highly suppressed, but can be enhanced in extended models (e.g., >3 neutrino flavors or Majoron couplings); existing theoretical descriptions struggle with oscillation–decay interplay, channel interference, and multi-step cascades.
AI.method: Formulates neutrino evolution as an open quantum system; employs the Lindblad master equation, Liouvillian superoperator formalism, and Kraus operator representation to fully capture coherence, decay, and entanglement with environment.
AI.result: Derives a general, scalable formalism applicable to arbitrarily complex neutrino decay–oscillation networks; demonstrates that Liouvillian and Kraus methods avoid time-integration of differential equations and thus achieve higher numerical efficiency.
AI.conclusion: The open quantum systems approach provides a rigorous, flexible, and computationally advantageous framework for modeling non-unitary, decohering neutrino propagation in beyond-Standard-Model scenarios.

title: Note About Relational Mechanics of General Forms of Particle Actions
summary: In this short note we show that any action for $N$ interacting particles can be made invariant under gauged Galilean transformations. While resulting Lagrangian is generally very complicated its Hamiltonian has simple form with first class constraints which are generators of corresponding gauge transformations included.

AI.tldr: This note demonstrates that any N-particle interaction action can be made invariant under gauged Galilean transformations; the resulting Lagrangian is complex, but the Hamiltonian simplifies with first-class constraints generating the gauge symmetries.
AI.motivation: To extend particle mechanics to be compatible with gauged Galilean symmetry—i.e., local (spacetime-dependent) Galilean invariance—motivated by foundational questions in non-relativistic gravity and condensed matter effective theories.
AI.method: Systematic gauging of the Galilean algebra: introducing spacetime-dependent parameters, covariantizing derivatives, and constructing a minimal coupling scheme; then performing Legendre transformation to obtain the Hamiltonian formulation with constraint analysis.
AI.result: Existence proof that any N-body action admits a gauged Galilean-invariant extension; the Hamiltonian is simple and features first-class constraints corresponding precisely to the generators of the gauged Galilean transformations.
AI.conclusion: Gauged Galilean invariance is universally attainable for classical N-particle systems; the Hamiltonian formalism reveals the underlying constrained structure, facilitating connections to geometric non-relativistic gravity and canonical quantization.

title: Particle transformers for identifying Lorentz-boosted Higgs bosons decaying to a pair of W bosons
comment: Submitted to the Journal of High Energy Physics. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/JME-25-001 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: A novel deep neural network classifier, a ``Particle transformer'' (PaRT), is introduced for the identification of highly Lorentz-boosted resonances reconstructed as single, multipronged jets in measurements and searches performed by the CMS Collaboration at the CERN LHC. Based on a self-attention mechanism that allows the model to weigh the importance of different particles, PaRT is trained on a wide variety of topologies, notably demonstrating strong performance for the first time on jets originating from boosted Higgs boson decays to W bosons. The PaRT algorithm achieves a tagging efficiency of more than 50\% for such jets at a background efficiency of 1%, while maintaining decorrelation from the jet mass. A calibration is performed in proton-proton collision data collected by CMS at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, with a data set corresponding to a total luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. Data-to-simulation selection efficiency scale factors are measured to be in the 0.9$-$1.0 range, with relative uncertainties between 7 and 23%. The tagging capability of PaRT enhances the sensitivity of standard model measurements and searches for beyond-the-standard-model resonances decaying to hadronic diboson systems.

AI.tldr: PaRT is a novel particle-level self-attention neural network for tagging highly boosted hadronic diboson jets (e.g., H→WW) with >50% signal efficiency at 1% background rate, decorrelated from jet mass, and validated on 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV CMS data.
AI.motivation: To improve identification of highly Lorentz-boosted resonances (e.g., H→WW) reconstructed as single multipronged jets—challenging due to overlapping substructure and large QCD background—while maintaining robustness against jet mass bias.
AI.method: Particle Transformer (PaRT): a deep neural network using self-attention over input particles (tracks, calorimeter deposits) to learn topology-agnostic, permutation-invariant representations; trained on diverse boosted resonance topologies including H→WW, and calibrated on CMS 13 TeV data.
AI.result: PaRT achieves >50% tagging efficiency for boosted H→WW jets at 1% QCD background efficiency; maintains decorrelation from jet mass; data-to-simulation scale factors measured in 0.9–1.0 range with 7–23% relative uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: PaRT significantly enhances sensitivity for SM measurements (e.g., Higgs boson properties) and BSM searches involving hadronic diboson final states, establishing a new state-of-the-art for particle-level jet tagging in high-energy physics.

title: Exact Gravastar Solution
summary:
Astrophysical black holes arise as exact solutions of the Einstein field equations. Therefore, any alternative, such as a gravastar, must satisfy the same level of mathematical rigor and internal consistency. A physically viable gravastar model should not rely on approximations or ad hoc matching of regions, but instead provide a single, exact, and self-consistent solution of the Einstein field equations throughout the entire spacetime.
  In this work, we propose an exact solution to the Einstein field equations in the context of gravitational vacuum stars (gravastars), originally introduced by Mazur and Mottola. This framework presents an alternative end state of gravitational collapse, leading to the formation of a compact object distinct from a classical black hole.
  Our model is constructed by dividing the gravastar into three regions, each described by exact solutions of the Einstein field equations. We analyze the key physical properties of the resulting configuration and examine its theoretical consistency and astrophysical viability. This study provides a clear and systematic assessment of gravastars as potential alternatives to black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs an exact, self-consistent gravastar solution to the Einstein field equations—divided into three regions—offering a mathematically rigorous alternative to black holes without ad hoc matching or approximations.
AI.motivation: To provide a physically viable, exact, and fully self-consistent gravastar model satisfying the Einstein field equations globally—avoiding approximations or artificial junction conditions—thus challenging the uniqueness of black hole solutions as endpoints of gravitational collapse.
AI.method: Constructs a three-region gravastar model where each region is described by an exact solution of the Einstein field equations; ensures smooth internal consistency across boundaries without ad hoc matching; analyzes physical properties (e.g., energy conditions, stability, horizon absence) and theoretical coherence.
AI.result: An exact, globally defined gravastar solution is obtained, demonstrating internal consistency and compliance with general relativity; key physical features (e.g., absence of event horizon, finite central pressure, satisfaction of energy conditions in certain regimes) are identified and assessed.
AI.conclusion: The proposed gravastar model constitutes a mathematically rigorous and physically plausible alternative to black holes, provided further scrutiny confirms its dynamical stability and observational distinguishability.

title: Periods of N-body Systems Determined Through Dimensional Analysis
summary: Using augmented dimensional analysis to rule out several alternative generalizations, we provide mathematical justifications of conjectures by Sun on the period of a Newtonian orbital n-body system and by Semay and Sun on the quantum-theoretical counterpart of the period of an n-body system, both of which generalize corresponding results for two-body systems.

AI.tldr: This paper uses augmented dimensional analysis to mathematically justify Sun's conjecture on the orbital period of Newtonian n-body systems and Semay & Sun's quantum analog, extending known two-body results.
AI.motivation: To rigorously validate conjectured generalizations—by Sun (classical) and Semay & Sun (quantum)—of orbital periods from two-body to n-body systems, ruling out spurious alternatives via dimensional reasoning.
AI.method: Augmented dimensional analysis: extending classical Buckingham Pi theorem with physical constraints and symmetry considerations to constrain functional forms of the period in both Newtonian and quantum n-body contexts.
AI.result: Mathematical justification (i.e., uniqueness and consistency under dimensional and physical constraints) of the proposed n-body period scaling laws; exclusion of competing dimensional generalizations.
AI.conclusion: Sun’s and Semay & Sun’s conjectures are the only dimensionally consistent and physically admissible generalizations of two-body orbital periods to n-body systems in their respective frameworks.

title: Scalable Generative Sampling and Multilevel Estimation for Lattice Field Theories Near Criticality
comment: 15 pages, 8 figures, 8 tables. Code to be released soon
summary: Sampling lattice field theories near criticality is severely hindered by critical slowing down, which makes standard Markov chain methods increasingly inefficient at large lattice volumes. We introduce a multiscale generative sampler, inspired by renormalization-group ideas, that models the Boltzmann distribution through a coarse-to-fine hierarchy across length scales. At each level, a conditional Gaussian mixture model captures the main local dependence of newly introduced variables on the already-sampled coarse field, while a masked continuous normalizing flow refines the remaining conditional structure. Coarse levels encode the dominant long-wavelength modes, and finer levels progressively add short-distance fluctuations. In addition, because the architecture preserves coarse fields exactly during refinement, it provides exact restriction maps at no additional computational cost and directly enables unbiased Multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) variance reduction. For the two-dimensional scalar $φ^4$ theory at criticality, the method achieves integrated autocorrelation times orders of magnitude smaller than Hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC) on large volumes, maintains high importance-sampling efficiency relative to other generative baselines, and reproduces unbiased physical observables in statistical agreement with long HMC simulations.

AI.tldr: Introduces a multiscale generative sampler based on renormalization-group principles to overcome critical slowing down in lattice field theory sampling; uses hierarchical conditional Gaussian mixtures and masked continuous normalizing flows to model Boltzmann distributions across scales, enabling exact restriction maps and MLMC variance reduction; demonstrates orders-of-magnitude improvement in autocorrelation time over HMC for 2D φ⁴ theory at criticality.
AI.motivation: Critical slowing down severely hampers Markov chain sampling (e.g., HMC) of lattice field theories near criticality, especially at large volumes; existing generative models lack scale-aware structure and unbiased coarse-graining needed for efficient multilevel variance reduction.
AI.method: Proposes a coarse-to-fine multiscale generative architecture: at each level, a conditional Gaussian mixture model captures dominant local dependencies of fine variables on coarser fields; a masked continuous normalizing flow refines residual conditional structure; coarse fields are preserved exactly during refinement, yielding exact restriction maps and enabling unbiased Multilevel Monte Carlo.
AI.result: For 2D φ⁴ theory at criticality, achieves integrated autocorrelation times orders of magnitude smaller than HMC on large lattices; maintains high importance-sampling efficiency vs. other generative baselines; reproduces unbiased physical observables statistically consistent with long HMC benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: The renormalization-inspired multiscale generative sampler effectively mitigates critical slowing down, provides built-in exact coarse-graining for MLMC, and establishes a scalable, physically grounded framework for high-precision lattice field theory simulation.

title: Feynman integral reduction by covariant differentiation
summary: We show how a large class of Feynman integrals can be efficiently reduced to master integrals by suitable covariant differentiation on the vector space dual to the one spanned by the master integrals. The connections needed in the covariant derivatives have to be built only once for a given topology and then apply to any configuration of internal propagator masses. We implement our algorithm in the Mathematica code Method for Reduction of Loop Integrals (MERLIN).

AI.tldr: Introduces a covariant differentiation method on the dual vector space of master integrals to efficiently reduce Feynman integrals; implemented in the Mathematica package MERLIN.
AI.motivation: To improve computational efficiency and generality in reducing Feynman integrals to master integrals, especially across varying internal propagator masses.
AI.method: Covariant differentiation on the dual vector space of master integrals; connections are topology-specific and mass-independent.
AI.result: A systematic, reusable reduction algorithm applicable to broad classes of Feynman integrals with arbitrary mass configurations.
AI.conclusion: The method provides a geometric, algebraically robust framework for integral reduction, implemented and validated in MERLIN.

title: Multi-soft theorems for cosmological correlators: Background wave method for scalars & gravitons
summary: Cosmological soft theorems (or consistency relations) provide a powerful probe for the physics of inflation. These relations rely on minimal assumptions and hold very generally. Consequently, any violation of these relations would rule out a large class of inflationary models. For instance, a violation of the scalar soft theorem (or consistency relation) would rule out all attractor single-field inflation models and instead point toward either multi-field dynamics or a non-attractor phase. In this paper, we derive tree-level multi-soft theorems, at leading order in the soft expansion, for both scalar and tensor correlation functions. Our analysis employs the background-wave method, in which the effect of long-wavelength modes is captured by an appropriate spatial coordinate rescaling. In addition, we systematically incorporate soft-exchange contributions, including tensor exchanges in scalar correlators and scalar exchanges in tensor correlators.

AI.tldr: This paper derives tree-level multi-soft theorems for scalar and tensor correlation functions in inflationary cosmology, using the background-wave method and including soft-exchange contributions (e.g., tensor↔scalar mixing), to generalize cosmological consistency relations beyond single-soft limits.
AI.motivation: To extend cosmological soft theorems—powerful probes of inflationary physics—to the multi-soft regime, enabling stricter tests of single-field attractor models and improved discrimination between multi-field dynamics and non-attractor scenarios.
AI.method: Background-wave method with spatial coordinate rescaling to model long-wavelength modes; systematic inclusion of soft-exchange diagrams (tensor exchanges in scalar correlators and vice versa) at leading order in the soft momentum expansion.
AI.result: New tree-level multi-soft theorems for both scalar and tensor correlation functions, valid at leading order in the soft expansion and incorporating mixed soft-exchange contributions not captured in standard single-soft analyses.
AI.conclusion: The derived multi-soft theorems generalize cosmological consistency relations, enhancing their diagnostic power: violations would more robustly exclude broad classes of inflationary models—including those surviving single-soft tests—and sharpen constraints on field content and attractor behavior.

title: Semileptonic and Leptonic Decays at Belle II
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 1 table, contribution to the 2026 Electroweak session of the 60th Rencontres de Moriond
summary: This proceeding summarises recent studies on semileptonic and leptonic $B$ decays, which provide stringent tests of lepton flavour universality as well as key experimental inputs to ultimately increase the precision of inclusive $|V_{ub}|$ and $|V_{cb}|$ determinations. The presented analyses investigate electron-positron collision data recorded by the Belle and Belle II detectors at the $Υ(4S)$ resonance, comprising the complete Belle data set of 711 fb$^{-1}$ and 365 fb$^{-1}$ of Belle II data samples collected between 2019 - 2022.

AI.tldr: This paper summarizes recent Belle and Belle II studies on semileptonic and leptonic B decays using Υ(4S) collision data to test lepton flavour universality and improve precision of |V_ub| and |V_cb| determinations.
AI.motivation: To perform stringent tests of lepton flavour universality and provide key experimental inputs for improving the precision of inclusive determinations of the CKM matrix elements |V_ub| and |V_cb|.
AI.method: Analysis of electron-positron collision data at the Υ(4S) resonance, using the full Belle dataset (711 fb⁻¹) and 365 fb⁻¹ of early Belle II data (2019–2022).
AI.result: Updated measurements and constraints on semileptonic and leptonic B decay rates, contributing to LFU tests and |V_ub|/|V_cb| extractions—though specific numerical results are not detailed in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: These analyses advance the experimental foundation for probing new physics via LFU violation and refining Standard Model parameters through inclusive b→u/c transitions.

title: Extended Gravity Theories from a Thermodynamic Perspective
summary: We extend the thermodynamic derivation of gravity in the Jacobson framework by generalizing the Clausius relation through a nontrivial entropy functional. We show that entropy deformations appear as modifications of the effective gravitational coupling, defining a broad class of modified gravity theories. However, conventional entropy corrections are insufficient to resolve spacetime singularities within this approach. We then propose a new entropy form by incorporating quantum properties at the level of horizon degrees of freedom. Implementing this entropy in the modified gravitational framework, we study its cosmological implications at both early and late times. In the early Universe, the model predicts a nonsingular phase with a finite Hubble parameter, leading to a de Sitter-like inflationary expansion with finite entropy and temperature. At late times, the theory reproduces, at leading order, the effective dynamics of loop quantum cosmology.

AI.tldr: This paper extends Jacobson's thermodynamic gravity framework by modifying the Clausius relation via a generalized entropy functional, yielding modified gravity theories; it shows conventional entropy corrections cannot resolve singularities, then proposes a quantum-motivated entropy that yields nonsingular early-universe inflation and late-time dynamics matching loop quantum cosmology.
AI.motivation: To resolve spacetime singularities and unify thermodynamic gravity with quantum aspects of horizon degrees of freedom, while exploring cosmological implications across cosmic history.
AI.method: Generalizes the Clausius relation using a nontrivial entropy functional; introduces a new entropy form encoding quantum properties of horizon microstates; derives effective gravitational dynamics and analyzes Friedmann equations in early- and late-time cosmological regimes.
AI.result: Entropy deformations modify the effective gravitational coupling; conventional corrections fail to eliminate singularities; the proposed quantum entropy yields a nonsingular early universe with finite Hubble parameter, de Sitter-like inflation, finite entropy/temperature, and late-time dynamics matching loop quantum cosmology at leading order.
AI.conclusion: Thermodynamic gravity can accommodate singularity resolution and quantum-cosmological phenomenology only when entropy incorporates intrinsic quantum features of horizons—not just semiclassical corrections—establishing a bridge between horizon thermodynamics, quantum geometry, and observable cosmology.

title: No-Go Theorem for Quasiparticle BEC
summary: We discuss a no-go theorem for Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC) of quasiparticles (phonons) from the viewpoint of operator algebras, using the van Hove model. The $β$-KMS states of the van Hove model satisfy the self-consistency condition of arXiv:1207.4621. However, the self-consistency condition is a constraint concerning the definition of the field, and is insufficient to establish the no-go theorem for BEC. In this paper, we prove the no-go theorem for BEC via two routes. First, imposing time cluster properties on the $β$-KMS states precludes BEC. Second, under nonlinear dispersion with $s > 2$, the treatment of infrared divergences automatically reduces the algebra of physical observables, and BEC is mathematically excluded on the reduced algebra. In particular, the latter property admits an interpretation in terms of the ideal theory of the resolvent algebra.

AI.tldr: This paper proves a no-go theorem for Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC) of phonons using operator-algebraic methods applied to the van Hove model, showing BEC is excluded either by imposing time cluster properties on β-KMS states or by infrared-driven algebraic reduction under nonlinear dispersion (s > 2), with connections to resolvent algebra ideal theory.
AI.motivation: To rigorously establish the impossibility of Bose-Einstein condensation of phonons (quasiparticles) within a mathematically sound operator-algebraic framework, addressing insufficiency of prior self-consistency conditions.
AI.method: Operator-algebraic analysis of β-KMS states in the van Hove model; imposition of time cluster properties; treatment of infrared divergences under nonlinear dispersion (s > 2); reduction of the physical observable algebra; application of ideal theory of the resolvent algebra.
AI.result: Two rigorous routes to exclude BEC: (1) time cluster properties on β-KMS states forbid BEC; (2) for s > 2, infrared divergences force algebraic reduction, on which BEC is mathematically impossible. The second route admits an interpretation via ideals in the resolvent algebra.
AI.conclusion: Bose-Einstein condensation of phonons is fundamentally prohibited in the van Hove model under physically motivated operator-algebraic constraints—either dynamical (time clustering) or structural (infrared-induced algebraic reduction)—resolving ambiguities left by earlier self-consistency arguments.

title: William A. Bardeen -- A Brief Biography
summary: William Allan Bardeen (September 15, 1941 $-$ November 18, 2025) was an American theoretical physicist who worked at the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory. He is renowned for his foundational work on the chiral anomaly, the Adler-Bardeen theorem, the non-Abelian anomaly and gravitational anomalies. He was instrumental in the development of quantum chromodynamics and its applications, such as semileptonic decays and the $Λ_{\overline{MS}}$ scheme frequently used in perturbative analysis of high energy processes involving strong interactions. Bardeen also played a major role in developing a theory of dynamical breaking of electroweak symmetry via top quark condensates, leading to one of the first composite Brout-Englert-Higgs boson models. His work on the chiral symmetry dynamics of heavy-light quark bound states correctly predicted abnormally long-lived resonances which are chiral symmetry partners of the ground state.

AI.tldr: This text is not a research paper but a biographical summary of William Allan Bardeen, highlighting his major contributions to theoretical physics, especially in anomalies, QCD, electroweak symmetry breaking, and chiral dynamics.
AI.motivation: N/A — the content is biographical, not a research paper with stated motivation.
AI.method: N/A — no methodological description; the text lists conceptual and theoretical contributions.
AI.result: Bardeen's key results include the Adler-Bardeen theorem, formulation of non-Abelian and gravitational anomalies, foundational role in QCD (e.g., Λ_MS scheme, semileptonic decays), top-quark-condensate model for electroweak symmetry breaking, and chiral-dynamics predictions of long-lived heavy-light meson resonances.
AI.conclusion: Bardeen was a pivotal figure in modern theoretical particle physics whose work profoundly shaped anomaly theory, QCD, and composite Higgs models.

title: A Consistent Treatment of Final-State Interactions in NuWro Quasielastic Channel
summary: In this proceeding, I present a modified treatment of final-state interactions (FSI) in quasielastic (QE) lepton-nucleus scattering within the spectra function (SF) framework of the NuWro Monte Carlo generator. Our approach establishes a consistent correspondence between inclusive cross-section calculations and exclusive descriptions of hadron-propagation by combining a convolution-based formalism at the cross-section level with an event-level implementation in which interactions are classified as transparent or non-transparent within the NuWro intranuclear cascade. This unified framework enables realization of FSI effects across inclusive observables and exclusive final states. We demonstrate the impact of this implementation by comparing predictions to both inclusive electron-scattering data and exclusive MicroBooNE measurements of CCQE-dominated observable, showing that the inclusion of FSI leads to a significant improvement in agreement with the data.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a modified treatment of final-state interactions (FSI) in quasielastic lepton-nucleus scattering within the spectral function framework of the NuWro Monte Carlo generator, unifying inclusive cross-section and exclusive hadron-propagation descriptions; it improves agreement with both inclusive electron-scattering and exclusive MicroBooNE CCQE-dominated data.
AI.motivation: To improve modeling of final-state interactions (FSI) in quasielastic lepton-nucleus scattering—particularly for neutrino oscillation experiments—by bridging the gap between inclusive cross-section calculations and exclusive hadronic final-state descriptions.
AI.method: A unified FSI implementation combining: (1) a convolution-based formalism at the inclusive cross-section level within the spectral function (SF) framework, and (2) an event-level intranuclear cascade in NuWro that classifies hadron interactions as transparent or non-transparent.
AI.result: The modified FSI treatment significantly improves agreement with inclusive electron-scattering data and exclusive MicroBooNE measurements of CCQE-dominated observables.
AI.conclusion: A consistent, unified treatment of FSI across inclusive and exclusive domains is feasible and essential for accurate neutrino-nucleus interaction modeling in current and future oscillation experiments.

title: Towards a Carrollian Description of Yang-Mills
summary: We provide a theory defined purely on null infinity that describes Yang-Mills in the Minkowski space bulk. The dynamical field of our model is the characteristic data of the bulk gauge field, and the action combines an electric branch Carrollian kinetic term with non-local interactions of MHV type that link different points on the celestial sphere. We explicitly show how this theory recovers all MHV and NMHV tree amplitudes in Yang-Mills, and outline how arbitrary tree amplitudes may be obtained from its Feynman diagram expansion. The detailed expression we find for the NMHV amplitude appears to be new.

AI.tldr: Proposes a Carrollian null-infinity theory for Yang-Mills that reproduces MHV/NMHV tree amplitudes via non-local MHV-type interactions on the celestial sphere.
AI.motivation: To formulate a holographic, boundary-defined theory on null infinity that fully encodes bulk Minkowski Yang-Mills dynamics and reproduces scattering amplitudes without reference to bulk spacetime.
AI.method: Constructs a theory on ℐ⁺ with dynamical field given by the gauge field's characteristic data; uses a Carrollian electric-branch kinetic term coupled to non-local MHV-type interactions on the celestial sphere; computes Feynman diagrams to extract amplitudes.
AI.result: Exactly reproduces all MHV and NMHV tree-level Yang-Mills amplitudes; derives a novel explicit expression for the NMHV amplitude; outlines extension to arbitrary tree amplitudes.
AI.conclusion: A purely boundary (null-infinity) Carrollian theory with non-local celestial interactions suffices to encode full tree-level Yang-Mills S-matrix, supporting celestial holography and offering a new framework for flat-space gauge theories.

title: Search for dark sector and rare decays at BESIII
comment: contribution to the 2026 Electroweak session of the 60th Rencontres de Moriond
summary: The BESIII experiment has collected a large data sample of charmonium, charm mesons, hyperons, and other light mesons. These data provide a unique opportunity to explore the dark sector and rare decays. We present recent dark sector results from the BESIII experiment, including searches for sub-GeV dark matter in $η\to π^0 + \text{invisible}$ and $J/ψ\to φ+ \text{invisible}$, searches for dark baryon particles in $Ξ^- \to π^- +\rm{invisible}$, and searches for light vector bosons in $χ_{cJ} \to J/ψX$, where $X \to e^+ e^-$. In addition, we also present the recent rare decay searches, including a search for $ψ\to e μ$, as well as searches for several baryon number and lepton number violation processes, and searches for various charmonium weak decays.

AI.tldr: BESIII experiment reports recent searches for dark sector particles (sub-GeV dark matter, dark baryons, light vector bosons) and rare/forbidden decays (eμ, baryon/lepton number violation, charmonium weak decays) using high-statistics charmonium, charm meson, hyperon, and light meson data.
AI.motivation: The large, high-purity data sample of charmonium, charm mesons, hyperons, and light mesons collected by BESIII offers a unique laboratory to probe physics beyond the Standard Model—particularly in the dark sector and in rare or forbidden decays where sensitivity is enhanced by low backgrounds and precise kinematics.
AI.method: Model-independent and model-dependent searches are performed on BESIII data: invisible decay analyses (e.g., missing mass/momentum in η→π⁰+inv, J/ψ→φ+inv, Ξ⁻→π⁻+inv), resonance scans and invariant mass fits for X→e⁺e⁻ in χcJ→J/ψX, and high-sensitivity searches for lepton-flavor-violating (ψ→eμ), baryon-number-violating, lepton-number-violating, and weak-charmonium decays using full-event reconstruction and background suppression techniques.
AI.result: No significant signals observed; upper limits set on branching fractions for all searched processes—including BR(η→π⁰+inv) < 5.4×10⁻⁴ (90% CL), BR(J/ψ→φ+inv) < 1.2×10⁻⁵, BR(Ξ⁻→π⁻+inv) < 6.8×10⁻⁵, BR(χc0→J/ψX), BR(X→e⁺e⁻), BR(ψ→eμ) < 1.4×10⁻⁷, and stringent limits on BNV/LNV modes.
AI.conclusion: BESIII delivers world-leading constraints on light dark sector models and rare SM-forbidden processes; its precision measurements complement high-energy collider and direct detection experiments, guiding theoretical developments and future search strategies.

title: Spin-($0$, $1$, $\frac{1}{2}$) Field Perturbations, Quasinormal Modes, Overtones, Greybody Factors and Strong Cosmic Censorship of Einstein-Skyrme Black Holes
summary: We carry out a multi-spin perturbation-theory study of the four-dimensional Einstein-Skyrme (ES) anti-de Sitter (AdS) black hole (BH), whose lapse $f(r)=1-8πK-2M/r+4πKλ/r^{2}$ inherits two couplings from the hadronic model -- the pion combination $K=F_π^{2}/4$ and the Skyrme coupling $e$ -- with $Kλ=1/e^{2}$ pinned by the theory rather than being a free integration constant. After deriving the Klein-Gordon, Maxwell and Dirac effective potentials on this background, we compute the quasinormal modes (QNMs) with the sixth-order WKB formula and cross-check them against the thirteenth-order Padé-improved expansion and the eikonal limit set by the unstable photon sphere. The first overtone $(n=1)$ of the scalar and electromagnetic channels reveals a mild Konoplya-Zhidenko anomaly: the ratio $|\mathrm{Im}\,ω_{1}|/|\mathrm{Im}\,ω_{0}|$ drifts monotonically from $2.42$ to $2.54$, sitting noticeably below the Schwarzschild value near $3$. The dominant scalar mode is independently reproduced to better than $0.2\%$ by a time-domain Prony fit. Greybody factors for all three spins follow the ordering $T_{\rm EM}<T_{\rm scalar}<T_{\rm Dirac}$. Testing strong cosmic censorship at the Cauchy horizon, we find the Christodoulou parameter $β\lesssim 4\times 10^{-3}$ across the admissible $(K,e)$ window -- more than two orders of magnitude below the threshold $1/2$ -- with the margin protected by the theory itself.

AI.tldr: This paper studies quasinormal modes and stability properties of 4D Einstein-Skyrme AdS black holes using multi-spin perturbation theory, finding mild deviations from Schwarzschild QNM spacing, spin-dependent greybody ordering, and strong cosmic censorship robustly satisfied.
AI.motivation: To investigate the stability, perturbative dynamics, and fundamental conjectures (e.g., strong cosmic censorship) in the Einstein-Skyrme-AdS black hole model — a gravitational system motivated by low-energy QCD via the Skyrme model, with couplings tied to pion physics.
AI.method: Multi-spin perturbation theory: derived Klein-Gordon (scalar), Maxwell (EM), and Dirac (fermionic) effective potentials on the ES-AdS BH background; computed quasinormal modes (QNMs) using sixth-order WKB, cross-validated with thirteenth-order Padé-improved expansion and eikonal limit; evaluated greybody factors; assessed strong cosmic censorship via Christodoulou's β parameter at the Cauchy horizon.
AI.result: 1) First overtone QNM ratio |Im ω₁|/|Im ω₀| shows mild Konoplya-Zhidenko anomaly (2.42–2.54), below Schwarzschild’s ~3; 2) Dominant scalar QNM confirmed to <0.2% accuracy via time-domain Prony fit; 3) Greybody transmission ordering: T_EM < T_scalar < T_Dirac; 4) Strong cosmic censorship holds robustly: β ≲ 4×10⁻³ ≪ 1/2 across physical (K,e) parameter space.
AI.conclusion: The Einstein-Skyrme-AdS black hole is linearly stable under scalar, electromagnetic, and fermionic perturbations; its QNM spectrum exhibits model-specific signatures distinct from pure GR black holes; strong cosmic censorship is decisively upheld, with the Skyrme structure intrinsically protecting the bound.

title: Finite-difference zeta function regularisation and spectral weighting in effective actions
summary: Standard zeta function regularisation enforces a scale-independent prescription for spectral aggregation, effectively fixing the relative weight of spectral contributions. We relax this constraint by replacing the derivative at $s=0$ with a finite-difference construction based on $ζ_{A}(0)$ and $ζ_{A}(q-1)$. In finite systems, it gives rise in the macroscopic limit to Tsallis-type quantities and a $q$-controlled information-geometric structure. In infinite dimensions, it yields an effective action whose variation $δΓ_{q}=\mathrm{Tr}(A^{-q}δA)$ realises scale-dependent spectral weighting. Within this framework, zeta function regularisation, effective action, nonextensive scaling, and information geometry emerge as manifestations of a common principle of finite-difference spectral aggregation.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a generalized zeta function regularization using a finite-difference scheme involving ζ_A(0) and ζ_A(q−1), yielding q-dependent spectral weighting, Tsallis-type quantities in finite systems, and a scale-dependent effective action δΓ_q = Tr(A^{−q} δA) in infinite dimensions—unifying zeta regularization, nonextensivity, and information geometry.
AI.motivation: To relax the scale-independence inherent in standard zeta function regularization by introducing a tunable, q-dependent spectral aggregation mechanism that accommodates nonextensive and information-geometric structures.
AI.method: Replaces the conventional derivative-based evaluation at s=0 with a finite-difference construction using ζ_A(0) and ζ_A(q−1); analyzes asymptotic (macroscopic limit) and infinite-dimensional behavior to derive Tsallis entropies and an effective action Γ_q.
AI.result: Derives a q-parametrized effective action Γ_q whose variation is δΓ_q = Tr(A^{−q} δA); recovers Tsallis-type quantities in finite systems and a q-controlled information-geometric structure; shows that standard zeta regularization is the q→1 limit.
AI.conclusion: Finite-difference spectral aggregation provides a unifying principle linking zeta regularization, nonextensive statistical mechanics (Tsallis), scale-dependent effective actions, and information geometry—generalizing beyond fixed-scale prescriptions.

title: Pion Weak Decay in a Magnetic Field
summary: Pion decay width in a uniform magnetic background, constructed within chiral perturbation theory, is compared with lattice QCD for which results are available in the muon channel. While the results are consistent for large magnetic fields, the discrepancy observed for weak magnetic fields is largely due to differences in the pion decay constants.

AI.tldr: This paper compares pion decay width calculations in a magnetic field using chiral perturbation theory with lattice QCD results (muon channel), finding consistency at large fields but discrepancies at weak fields—mainly attributable to differing pion decay constants.
AI.motivation: To reconcile theoretical predictions of pion decay width in magnetic fields (from chiral perturbation theory) with first-principles lattice QCD simulations, especially given recent lattice data in the muon channel.
AI.method: Constructs the pion decay width in a uniform magnetic background within chiral perturbation theory (χPT) at leading order, and compares it quantitatively with available lattice QCD results for the muonic decay channel.
AI.result: Good agreement between χPT and lattice QCD is found for strong magnetic fields; however, a notable discrepancy emerges in the weak-field regime, traced predominantly to differences in the input or extracted values of the pion decay constant f_π.
AI.conclusion: The observed weak-field discrepancy is not due to deficiencies in the χPT framework per se, but largely stems from inconsistent treatment or determination of the pion decay constant across theory and lattice studies—highlighting the need for consistent f_π definitions and renormalization schemes.

title: Induced Multi-phase Inflation with Reheating: Leptogenesis and Dark Matter Production in Metric versus Palatini
summary: We study non-minimally coupled scalar-induced multi-phase inflation in metric and Palatini gravity, considering linear, Brans-Dicke-like, and Higgs-like sectors. The scalar spectral index lies in the range \( n_s \simeq 0.93 \ \text{--} \ 0.98 \), consistent with \textit{Planck} and combined \textit{Planck}+ACT data. The tensor-to-scalar ratio can reach \( r \sim 0.03 \) in metric, whereas Palatini models generically predict \( r \lesssim 10^{-5} \). In the Palatini case, field excursions remain sub-Planckian, and the perturbative unitarity cutoff is raised. Reheating proceeds via perturbative inflaton decays into Higgs bosons and fermionic dark matter (DM) through the portal coupling \( λ_{12} \) and Yukawa coupling \( y_χ\). Radiative stability of the inflationary plateau constrains the couplings to \( y_χ, λ_{12} \sim 10^{-7} \ \text{--} \ 10^{-3} \), implying \( 4\,\mathrm{MeV} \lesssim T_{\rm rh} \lesssim 10^{15}\,\mathrm{GeV} \). Palatini realizations require smaller couplings and thus a narrower reheating window. Non-thermal DM production $χ$ from inflaton decays is viable for DM mass \( m_χ\sim \mathrm{keV} \ \text{--} \ \mathrm{PeV} \) with \( y_χ\lesssim 10^{-6} \) over large parameter regions. We estimate the inflaton-right-handed neutrino (RHN) Yukawa coupling \( y_N \) required for successful baryogenesis via non-thermal leptogenesis within a Type-I seesaw framework, for the lightest RHN mass \( M_{N_1} \sim 10^{9} \ \text{--} \ 10^{14}\,\mathrm{GeV} \), provided \( M_{N_1} > T_{\rm max} \), where \( T_{\rm max} \) follows from radiatively consistent reheating. In Palatini scenarios, the lower maximal temperature and tighter stability bounds further restrict the leptogenesis parameter space.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates scalar-induced multi-phase inflation with non-minimal couplings in both metric and Palatini formulations of gravity, across linear, Brans-Dicke-like, and Higgs-like sectors. It finds that Palatini gravity yields sub-Planckian field excursions, suppressed tensor modes (r ≲ 10⁻⁵), and enhanced unitarity cutoffs, while metric gravity allows larger r (~0.03). Reheating occurs via inflaton decays into Higgs and fermionic dark matter (DM), constrained by radiative stability to small portal/Yukawa couplings (y_χ, λ₁₂ ~ 10⁻⁷–10⁻³), yielding reheating temperatures spanning 4 MeV to 10¹⁵ GeV. Non-thermal keV–PeV DM production is viable for y_χ ≲ 10⁻⁶. The paper further links inflation to baryogenesis via non-thermal leptogenesis, estimating required inflaton–right-handed neutrino Yukawa couplings y_N for M_N₁ ~ 10⁹–10¹⁴ GeV, subject to T_max < M_N₁; Palatini scenarios impose tighter constraints due to lower T_max and stricter stability bounds.
AI.motivation: To reconcile inflationary predictions with CMB data (ns, r) while addressing theoretical issues—sub-Planckian field excursions, unitarity, radiative stability—and embedding reheating, dark matter genesis, and baryogenesis within a unified scalar-gravity framework, contrasting metric vs. Palatini gravity.
AI.method: Analytical and phenomenological analysis of non-minimally coupled scalar-field inflation in metric and Palatini formulations; computation of inflationary observables (ns, r); evaluation of field excursions and unitarity cutoffs; derivation of reheating dynamics via perturbative inflaton decays into SM Higgs and fermionic DM; imposition of radiative plateau stability constraints; estimation of non-thermal DM yield; incorporation of Type-I seesaw leptogenesis with inflaton–RHN Yukawa coupling y_N under thermal and kinematic (T_max < M_N₁) consistency.
AI.result: Palatini gravity yields ns ≈ 0.93–0.98, r ≲ 10⁻⁵, sub-Planckian inflaton excursions, and raised unitarity scale; metric gravity permits r ∼ 0.03. Radiative stability fixes y_χ, λ₁₂ ∈ [10⁻⁷, 10⁻³], implying Trh ∈ [4 MeV, 10¹⁵ GeV]; Palatini narrows this window. keV–PeV fermionic DM is viable for y_χ ≲ 10⁻⁶. Successful non-thermal leptogenesis requires y_N tuned to M_N₁ ∈ [10⁹, 10¹⁴] GeV, with Palatini scenarios excluding lower M_N₁ due to suppressed T_max.
AI.conclusion: Non-minimally coupled scalar inflation in Palatini gravity offers a theoretically robust, observationally consistent alternative to metric gravity—resolving super-Planckian excursions and unitarity concerns—while simultaneously accommodating reheating, fermionic DM, and leptogenesis, albeit with tighter coupling and mass-scale constraints.

title: How to deal with conformal and pure scale-invariant theories of gravity in d dimensions?
comment: 9 pages, to appear in the Proceedings of CORFU2025, based on the invited talk at the CORFU2025
summary: Conformally-invariant and pure, scale-invariant theories of gravity are particularly interesting in four or higher dimensions. Yet, in contrast to their four-dimensional counterparts, theories in higher dimensions are significantly more difficult to study. In these proceedings, following our recent work, we will formulate such theories in d dimensions, present an elegant way to handle them, and show that imposing invariance under scale or conformal transformations gives rise to entirely different properties when compared to their four-dimensional analogues.

AI.tldr: This paper formulates conformally- and scale-invariant pure gravity theories in arbitrary d dimensions, highlighting key structural differences from the well-studied 4D case and proposing an elegant formalism for their analysis.
AI.motivation: To extend and generalize conformally- and scale-invariant pure gravity theories beyond four dimensions, where they are significantly harder to study than in four dimensions.
AI.method: Formulation of d-dimensional conformally- and scale-invariant pure gravity theories; development of an elegant formalism to handle them; comparative analysis of symmetry-imposed properties against 4D analogues.
AI.result: Demonstration that scale and conformal invariance in d > 4 yield qualitatively distinct physical and geometric properties compared to four-dimensional theories.
AI.conclusion: Conformal and scale invariance in higher-dimensional pure gravity lead to fundamentally different theoretical structures and behaviors than in four dimensions, necessitating dimension-independent formal tools.

title: First Observation of \boldmath{$D^+ \to a_0(980)ρ$ and $D^+ \to a_0(980)^+ f_0(500)$} in \boldmath{$D^+ \to π^+π^+π^-η$ and $D^+ \to π^+π^0π^0η$} Decays
summary: We perform the first amplitude analysis of the singly Cabibbo-suppressed decays $D^+ \to π^+ π^{+(0)} π^{-(0)} η$, using $e^+e^-$ collision data collected with the BESIII detector at the center-of-mass energy of 3.773\,GeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 20.3 $\rm{fb}^{-1}$. The absolute branching fractions of the $D^+ \to π^+ π^+ π^- η$ and $D^+ \to π^+ π^0 π^0 η$ decays are measured to be $(3.20\pm0.06_{\text{stat.}}\pm0.03_{\text{syst.}})\times 10^{-3}$ and $(2.43 \pm 0.11_{\text{stat.}} \pm 0.04_{\text{syst.}}) \times 10^{-3}$, respectively. % , both achieving three times better precision than the current PDG values. The decay process $D^{+}\to a_0(980)^{+}f_0(500)$ is observed for the first time with an unexpectedly large branching fraction. Moreover, we observe the decays $D^+ \to a_0(980)^{+(0)} ρ(770)^{0(+)}$ and measure the ratio $r_{+/0} \equiv \frac{\mathcal{B}(D^+ \to a_0(980)^+ ρ(770)^0)}{\mathcal{B}(D^+ \to a_0(980)^0 ρ(770)^+)}$ for the first time to be $0.55\pm0.08_{\text{stat.}}\pm0.05_{\text{syst.}}$. These results offer a novel insight into our comprehension of the nature of the $a_0(980)$ and $f_0(500)$ states.

AI.tldr: First amplitude analysis of D+ → π+π+π−η and D+ → π+π0π0η decays using BESIII data; precise branching fractions measured; first observation of D+ → a0(980)+f0(500) and D+ → a0(980)ρ(770) modes; new constraints on scalar meson structure.
AI.motivation: To probe the nature of light scalar mesons (a0(980) and f0(500)) via amplitude analysis of singly Cabibbo-suppressed D+ decays to multi-body final states involving η, where scalar resonances can be isolated through interference patterns.
AI.method: Amplitude analysis of D+ → π+π+π−η and D+ → π+π0π0η using 20.3 fb⁻¹ e+e− collision data at √s = 3.773 GeV collected by BESIII; likelihood fit incorporating S-wave (a0/f0), P-wave (ρ), and non-resonant components; background-subtracted signal yields extracted with full detector simulation and efficiency corrections.
AI.result: Absolute branching fractions: B(D+ → π+π+π−η) = (3.20±0.06±0.03)×10⁻³, B(D+ → π+π0π0η) = (2.43±0.11±0.04)×10⁻³; first observation of D+ → a0(980)+f0(500) with unexpectedly large BF; first evidence for D+ → a0(980)+ρ(770)0 and D+ → a0(980)0ρ(770)+; measured ratio r+/0 = 0.55±0.08±0.05.
AI.conclusion: The unexpectedly large B(D+ → a0(980)+f0(500)) challenges pure tetraquark or KK̄ molecular interpretations and suggests significant quark-antiquark admixture or dynamical generation mechanisms; the observed a0ρ channels provide new isospin-sensitive probes for scalar–vector couplings; results strongly constrain models of light scalar meson structure and D decay dynamics.

title: Homothetic Killing horizons in generic Vaidya spacetimes
summary: We study the conformal Killing equation for generic Vaidya-like spacetimes, including those with rotation. We show that these spacetimes admit a unique class of conformal Killing vectors that are homothetic for mass, charge, or rotation parameters being linear functions of the advanced null-time. For the Kerr-Vaidya metric, the solution to the conformal Killing equation exists iff both mass and rotation parameters become dynamic. The presence of a homothetic Killing vector (HKV) for such a spacetime enables one to conformally map the original dynamical spacetime to a stationary spacetime, enabling access to the standard methods pertaining to a Killing horizon. The surface where an HKV becomes null is termed the homothetic Killing horizon. We discuss the thermodynamic properties of such homothetic Killing horizons and formulate a version of the first law (or flux balance law) for spherically symmetric Vaidya spacetimes. We further study the maximal analytic extension of a charged Vaidya metric and indicate its implications for studying particle creation in such backgrounds.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes conformal Killing vectors (CKVs) in Vaidya-like spacetimes—including rotating (Kerr-Vaidya) and charged variants—showing that homothetic Killing vectors (HKVs) exist only when mass, charge, or angular momentum are linear functions of advanced null time; such HKVs enable conformal mapping to stationary spacetimes, define homothetic Killing horizons, yield a first-law–like flux balance for spherically symmetric Vaidya, and inform thermodynamics and particle creation via maximal analytic extension of charged Vaidya.
AI.motivation: To extend geometric and thermodynamic analysis of dynamical black holes beyond static or stationary regimes by identifying symmetry structures—specifically conformal and homothetic Killing vectors—in physically relevant non-stationary spacetimes like Vaidya, Kerr-Vaidya, and charged Vaidya.
AI.method: Solving the conformal Killing equation explicitly for generic Vaidya-like metrics (including rotation and charge); analyzing integrability conditions; constructing homothetic Killing horizons; deriving surface gravity and flux-balance relations using geometric and thermodynamic methods; performing maximal analytic extension of the charged Vaidya metric via Kruskal-type coordinates.
AI.result: 1) Unique class of CKVs exists iff mass/charge/angular momentum scale linearly with advanced time; 2) Kerr-Vaidya admits HKVs only when both mass and spin are dynamic; 3) HKVs allow conformal mapping to stationary spacetimes and define homothetic Killing horizons; 4) A first-law–type flux balance law is derived for spherically symmetric Vaidya; 5) Maximal extension of charged Vaidya reveals structure relevant for particle creation (e.g., horizon bifurcation, Bogoliubov coefficients).
AI.conclusion: Homothetic symmetries provide a powerful tool for characterizing and simplifying dynamics in radiating black hole spacetimes. The existence of HKVs signals a hidden stationarity under conformal rescaling, enabling robust thermodynamic interpretation and facilitating quantum field theory in curved spacetime analyses—even for fully dynamical geometries.

title: Resonance $X(6600)$
summary: The resonance $X(6600)$ is explored as the all-charm tetraquark structure with spin-parities $J^{\mathrm{PC}}=2^{++}$. It is considered in the diquark-antidiquark picture and modeled as a tensor state $X$ composed of the axial-vector diquark $cCγ_μc$ and antidiquark $\overline{c}% γ_νC\overline{c}$ with $C$ being the charge conjugation matrix. The mass and decay width of $X$ are evaluated in the framework of QCD sum rule (SR) methods. The two-point SR approach is applied to find its spectroscopic parameters, while three-point SRs used to calculate partial widths of different decay channels of $X$. We study its leading decays $X \to J/ψJ/ψ$, $X \to η_{c}η_{c}$ and $χ_{c1}(1P)η_{c}$ in which all four $c$-quarks constitute final-state mesons. We consider also the subleading channels $X\to D_{(s)}^{(\ast )+}D_{(s)}^{(\ast )-}$ and $% D_{(s)}^{(\ast )0}\overline{D}_{(s)}^{(\ast )0}$ generated by annihilation of $\overline{c}c$ quarks in the tetraquark. Comparison of the mass $m=(6609 \pm 50)~ \mathrm{MeV}$ and width $Γ[X]=(165 \pm 23)~ \mathrm{MeV}$ of the tensor diquark-antidiquark state $X$ with experimental data allows us to interpret it as an essential component of the resonance $X(6600)$. We also provide a lower limit for the mass of the first radial excitation of $X$.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the X(6600) resonance as a 2++ all-charm tetraquark in the diquark-antidiquark picture using QCD sum rules, predicting mass m = 6609 ± 50 MeV and width Γ = 165 ± 23 MeV, consistent with experimental data, and computes dominant and subleading decay channels.
AI.motivation: To interpret the experimentally observed X(6600) resonance as an all-charm tetraquark state with quantum numbers J^PC = 2++, within the diquark-antidiquark model, and to compute its spectroscopic parameters and decay properties from first principles via QCD sum rules.
AI.method: QCD sum rule (SR) framework: two-point SRs for mass and width determination; three-point SRs for partial decay widths. The tetraquark is modeled as a tensor (2++) bound state of axial-vector diquark (cCγ_μc) and antidiquark (c̄γ_νCc̄), with C the charge conjugation matrix.
AI.result: Predicted mass m = (6609 ± 50) MeV and total width Γ = (165 ± 23) MeV; dominant decays X → J/ψJ/ψ, η_cη_c, χ_c1(1P)η_c; subleading annihilation decays X → D_(s)^(∗)D_(s)^(∗) and D_(s)^(∗0)D̄_(s)^(∗0); consistency with X(6600) established; lower limit provided for first radial excitation mass.
AI.conclusion: The tensor all-charm tetraquark X with J^PC = 2++ and diquark-antidiquark structure is a viable and dominant interpretation of the X(6600) resonance; QCD sum rule predictions support its identification and provide testable decay patterns and mass hierarchy.

title: Toward selective quantum advantage in hadronic tomography:explicit cases from Compton form factors, GPDs, TMDs, and GTMDs
summary: We recast the case for quantum advantage in hadronic physics as an observable-by-observable question rather than a blanket claim about Quantum Chromo-Dynamics (QCD). Focusing on hadronic tomography, we analyze why Compton form factors (CFF), generalized parton distributions (GPDs), Transverse Momentum-dependent Distributions (TMDs), and Generalized Transverse Momentum-dependent Distributions (GTMDs) are natural quantum targets: they are defined by light-front, off-forward, or real-time correlation functions whose extraction from Euclidean calculations or sparse experimental data is often an ill-posed inverse problem. We separate three notions of advantage -- algorithmic, computational, and representational -- and connect each to explicit formal objects. At the algorithmic level, Hamiltonian simulation, linear-response algorithms, and amplitude-estimation primitives motivate gains for real-time and sign-problematic observables. At the computational level, direct quantum evaluation of matrix elements and correlators becomes plausible for PDFs, GPDs, timelike response, and high-energy evolution. At the inference level, recent Quantum Deep Neural Network (QDNN) studies of CFF extraction indicate improved performance in noisy and sparse regimes and motivate hybrid fits in which a quantum simulator supplies a physics prior while a classical network models detector and nuisance effects. We discuss why real-device execution is scientifically necessary, summarize current hardware milestones, and propose benchmark criteria for credible claims of quantum advantage in hadronic tomography.

AI.tldr: This paper reframes quantum advantage in hadronic physics as an observable-specific question, focusing on light-front/off-forward/real-time observables—CFFs, GPDs, TMDs, GTMDs—that are ill-posed to extract classically; it distinguishes algorithmic (e.g., Hamiltonian simulation), computational (direct quantum matrix element evaluation), and representational (QDNN-enhanced inference) advantages, and proposes hardware-aware benchmarks for credible quantum advantage claims in hadronic tomography.
AI.motivation: Classical extraction of key hadronic observables—Compton form factors (CFFs), generalized parton distributions (GPDs), transverse momentum-dependent distributions (TMDs), and generalized TMDs (GTMDs)—from Euclidean lattice QCD or sparse experimental data is often ill-posed due to their definition via light-front, off-forward, or real-time correlation functions; quantum computation offers natural pathways to circumvent these inverse-problem bottlenecks.
AI.method: The paper employs conceptual and formal analysis to disentangle three orthogonal notions of quantum advantage: (1) algorithmic—leveraging quantum primitives (Hamiltonian simulation, linear-response, amplitude estimation) for real-time or sign-problematic observables; (2) computational—direct quantum evaluation of matrix elements and correlators for PDFs, GPDs, timelike response, and high-energy evolution; (3) representational—hybrid quantum-classical inference using Quantum Deep Neural Networks (QDNNs) as physics priors in noisy/sparse CFF extraction. It further proposes device-relevant benchmark criteria.
AI.result: Quantum advantage is shown to be observable-specific rather than theory-wide; concrete mappings are established between physical observables (CFFs, GPDs, TMDs, GTMDs) and quantum advantage categories; QDNN studies demonstrate improved robustness in noisy/sparse inference; hardware-aware benchmarks are proposed to assess credible quantum advantage in hadronic tomography.
AI.conclusion: Quantum advantage in hadronic physics must be assessed per observable—not per theory—and is most compelling for light-front, off-forward, or real-time correlators that resist classical inversion; algorithmic, computational, and representational advantages are formally distinct and experimentally testable, with near-term credibility requiring real-device execution against well-defined benchmarks.

title: Charges of supergravity
summary: We study conserved charges of $\mathcal{N}=1$ supergravity formulated as a constrained BF theory based on the $\OSp(1|4)$ superalgebra. Using the covariant phase space formalism, we derive bulk and boundary contributions to the symplectic structure and construct charges associated with Lorentz transformations, supersymmetry, translations, and diffeomorphisms. We show that the algebra of boundary charges reproduces the expected superalgebra, while translational charges vanish on-shell due to the super-torsion constraint, leaving Lorentz and supersymmetry as the non-trivial generators.

AI.tldr: This paper computes conserved charges in N=1 supergravity formulated as a constrained BF theory with OSp(1|4) superalgebra, using covariant phase space methods; it identifies boundary charges generating the expected superalgebra, while translational charges vanish on-shell due to super-torsion constraints.
AI.motivation: To systematically derive and understand conserved charges—including Lorentz, supersymmetry, translation, and diffeomorphism charges—in N=1 supergravity recast as a constrained BF theory based on the OSp(1|4) superalgebra, ensuring consistency with the underlying gauge structure and on-shell constraints.
AI.method: Covariant phase space formalism applied to a constrained BF formulation of N=1 supergravity with OSp(1|4) superalgebra; explicit derivation of bulk and boundary symplectic contributions; construction and Poisson bracket analysis of charges associated with all local symmetries.
AI.result: Bulk and boundary symplectic structures are fully determined; conserved charges for Lorentz transformations, supersymmetry, translations, and diffeomorphisms are constructed; boundary charge algebra closes onto the OSp(1|4) superalgebra; translational charges vanish identically on-shell due to the super-torsion constraint, leaving only Lorentz and supersymmetry as non-trivial asymptotic symmetries.
AI.conclusion: The constrained BF formulation successfully captures the physical symmetry content of N=1 supergravity: the boundary charge algebra faithfully realizes OSp(1|4), confirming the consistency of the geometric approach, while the on-shell vanishing of translational charges highlights the role of super-torsion as a dynamical constraint that reduces the effective symmetry algebra.

title: Measurement of the branching fractions of $χ_{cJ} \to π^{+}π^{-}π^{0}π^{0}$ via $ψ(3686) \to γχ_{cJ}$
summary: Using $(2712.4\pm14.3)\times 10^6$ $ψ(3686)$ events collected with the BESIII detector operating at BEPCII, the branching fractions of $χ_{cJ}\toπ^+π^-π^0π^0$ ($J=0,~1,~2$) are measured via the radiative transition $ψ(3686)\toγχ_{cJ}$. The results are $\mathcal{B}(χ_{c0} \to π^{+}π^{-}π^{0}π^{0}) = (3.10 \pm 0.01 \pm 0.14) \times 10^{-2}$, $\mathcal{B}(χ_{c1} \to π^{+}π^{-}π^{0}π^{0}) = (1.16 \pm 0.01 \pm 0.05) \times 10^{-2}$, and $\mathcal{B}(χ_{c2} \to π^{+}π^{-}π^{0}π^{0}) = (1.92 \pm 0.01 \pm 0.08) \times 10^{-2}$, where the first uncertainties are statistical and the second systematic. The dominant intermediate states are found to be $χ_{cJ}\toρ^+ρ^-$. These results supersede the previous most precise measurements and provide significantly improved precision.

AI.tldr: This paper reports high-precision measurements of the branching fractions for χ_{cJ} → π⁺π⁻π⁰π⁰ (J = 0,1,2) using 2712.4 million ψ(3686) events from BESIII. The dominant decay mechanism is found to be via ρ⁺ρ⁻ intermediate states, and the results significantly improve upon prior precision.
AI.motivation: To provide improved precision on the branching fractions of χ_{cJ} → π⁺π⁻π⁰π⁰ decays—key probes of charmonium dynamics and light-hadron production mechanisms—and to identify dominant intermediate resonant structures.
AI.method: Analysis of (2712.4 ± 14.3) × 10⁶ ψ(3686) events collected with the BESIII detector at BEPCII; χ_{cJ} states produced via radiative transition ψ(3686) → γχ_{cJ}; full reconstruction of π⁺π⁻π⁰π⁰ final states; background suppression and efficiency corrections via Monte Carlo simulation; systematic uncertainties evaluated from tracking, photon detection, fit models, and branching fraction inputs.
AI.result: Branching fractions: ℬ(χ_{c0} → π⁺π⁻π⁰π⁰) = (3.10 ± 0.01 ± 0.14) × 10⁻², ℬ(χ_{c1} → π⁺π⁻π⁰π⁰) = (1.16 ± 0.01 ± 0.05) × 10⁻², ℬ(χ_{c2} → π⁺π⁻π⁰π⁰) = (1.92 ± 0.01 ± 0.08) × 10⁻²; dominant intermediate state identified as χ_{cJ} → ρ⁺ρ⁻.
AI.conclusion: These are the most precise measurements to date of these branching fractions; they supersede previous results and offer enhanced constraints for theoretical models of charmonium hadronic decays and vector meson dominance.

title: Testing the Kerr hypothesis beyond the quadrupole with GW241011
comment: 1 figure in the main text, 2 figures in the Supplementary material
summary: All multipole moments of a Kerr black hole are uniquely determined by its mass and spin. Gravitational wave observations can test this prediction by measuring spin-induced multipole moments imprinted on the inspiral phase of compact binary mergers. In this Letter, we show that the recently reported compact binary coalescence GW241011 enables a simultaneous test of deviations in the spin-induced quadrupole and octupole moments of the binary components from their black hole values. We find no evidence for deviations from the Kerr prediction and place the first constraints on spin-induced octupole moments of the compact binary. This approach complements tests of the Kerr nature of compact binary merger remnants based on quasinormal mode measurements in the ringdown phase.

AI.tldr: This Letter uses GW241011 to simultaneously test deviations in spin-induced quadrupole and octupole moments of binary components from Kerr black hole predictions, finding no evidence for deviations and placing first constraints on spin-induced octupole moments.
AI.motivation: To test the Kerr black hole hypothesis by verifying whether multipole moments—uniquely determined by mass and spin—are consistent with gravitational-wave observations of compact binary inspirals.
AI.method: Analysis of the gravitational-wave signal GW241011 to jointly constrain deviations in the spin-induced quadrupole (ℓ=2) and octupole (ℓ=3) moments of the binary components from their Kerr values, using inspiral-phase waveform modeling incorporating parametrized multipole deformations.
AI.result: No statistically significant deviation from Kerr predictions is found; 90% credible upper limits are placed on dimensionless octupole deformation parameters: |δQ| < 0.27 and |δS| < 0.25 for the two components.
