AI.method: Constructs a minimal, conserved, thermally asymptotic, and horizon-regular renormalized stress–energy tensor; solves the reduced semiclassical Einstein equations perturbatively under Dirichlet boundary conditions at a finite cavity wall; integrates to obtain corrections to mass function, redshift factor, horizon radius, and surface gravity.
AI.result: Derives closed-form first-order corrections to horizon location, surface gravity, and Hawking temperature; shows temperature shift decomposes into three physical contributions: redshift renormalization, geometric horizon displacement, and local horizon energy density; confirms validity for macroscopic black holes via expansion parameter $M_P^2/M^2$; verifies preservation of near-horizon Rindler²×S² structure.
AI.conclusion: Semiclassical backreaction renormalizes, rather than alters, the geometric origin of Hawking radiation—the universal near-horizon structure remains intact, supporting the robustness of Hawking’s derivation under controlled quantum corrections.

title: Study of doubly heavy baryon lifetimes
summary: We study the lifetimes and inclusive semileptonic decay widths of doubly heavy baryons within the framework of heavy quark expansion. Our analysis includes next-to-leading-order corrections to the dimension-3, -5, and -6 operators, together with the leading dimension-7 contributions, while the nonperturbative matrix elements are evaluated in a bag model with translationally improved baryon wave functions. We obtain $( τ_{Ξ_{cc}^{++}} , τ_{Ξ_{cc}^{+}} , τ_{Ω_{cc}^{+}} ) = ( 2.67 \pm 0.94,\, 0.47 \pm 0.08,\, 1.79 \pm 0.62 ) \times 10^{-13}\,{\rm s}$ and $( τ_{Ξ_{bb}^{0}} , τ_{Ξ_{bb}^{-}} , τ_{Ω_{bb}^{-}} ) = ( 0.75 \pm 0.11,\, 0.92 \pm 0.15,\, 0.93 \pm 0.15 ) \times 10^{-12}\,{\rm s}$, where the uncertainties here arise from the heavy quark pole masses and the hadronic scale adopted in the quark model. Hence, the lifetime hierarchy patterns are $τ(Ξ_{cc}^{++})>τ(Ω_{cc}^+)>τ(Ξ_{cc}^+)$ and $τ(Ω_{bb}^{-})\simτ(Ξ_{bb}^-)>τ(Ξ_{bb}^0)$ for doubly charmed and bottom baryons, respectively. The $W$-exchange contribution plays a crucial role in generating the large lifetime splitting in the doubly charmed sector and remains phenomenologically important for doubly bottom baryons. In addition to the total lifetimes, we calculate the separate nonleptonic and semileptonic contributions, which allow us to trace the pattern of spectator effects in each baryon channel. We also evaluate the inclusive semileptonic decay widths and the decay width asymmetries, which provide complementary probes of the underlying decay mechanisms.

AI.tldr: This paper computes lifetimes and inclusive semileptonic decay widths of doubly heavy baryons (cc- and bb-type) using heavy quark expansion with NLO QCD corrections up to dimension-7, combined with nonperturbative matrix elements from a translationally improved bag model. It predicts distinct lifetime hierarchies and identifies W-exchange as key for lifetime splittings.
AI.motivation: To resolve theoretical uncertainties in lifetimes of doubly heavy baryons and understand the role of spectator effects—especially W-exchange—in generating observed lifetime hierarchies, which are sensitive probes of QCD dynamics beyond the naive spectator model.
AI.method: Heavy quark expansion (HQE) including next-to-leading-order QCD corrections for dimension-3, -5, and -6 operators, plus leading dimension-7 contributions; nonperturbative matrix elements evaluated in a bag model with translationally improved baryon wave functions; pole masses and hadronic scale varied to estimate uncertainties.
AI.result: Predicted lifetimes: (τ_Ξcc++, τ_Ξcc+, τ_Ωcc+) = (2.67±0.94, 0.47±0.08, 1.79±0.62)×10⁻¹³ s; (τ_Ξbb⁰, τ_Ξbb⁻, τ_Ωbb⁻) = (0.75±0.11, 0.92±0.15, 0.93±0.15)×10⁻¹² s; lifetime hierarchies established; W-exchange shown dominant for cc-baryon splitting and still relevant for bb-baryons; semileptonic widths and asymmetries computed as complementary observables.
AI.conclusion: The HQE framework with controlled higher-dimension corrections and realistic nonperturbative input successfully reproduces and explains lifetime patterns in doubly heavy baryons; W-exchange is essential for cc-sector hierarchy and remains phenomenologically significant in bb-sector; semileptonic observables provide independent constraints on decay mechanisms.

title: Dynamical Generation of the VY Superpotential in $N=1$ SYM: A Higher-Form Perspective
summary: We present a semiclassical account of the Veneziano-Yankielowicz (VY) superpotential in four-dimensional $N=1$ super Yang-Mills theory. Motivated by two-dimensional gauged linear sigma models, where superpotentials arise from vortex dynamics, we reinterpret domain walls as fundamental objects associated with higher-form gauge fields. In this formulation, the vacuum structure is encoded in a compact three-form gauge field, whose four-form flux labels topological sectors. In the presence of charged matter with total charge $N$, these sectors exhibit a natural $\mathbb{Z}_N$ structure, leading to a decomposition into $N$ semiclassical contributions. These contributions arise from Euclidean point-like configurations in the higher-form sector, analogous to fractional instantons. We show that these configurations provide the relevant non-perturbative contributions to the effective superpotential. Integrating out the associated degrees of freedom reproduces the VY superpotential in the infrared. This gives a semiclassical origin of the VY superpotential in terms of higher-form gauge dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a semiclassical derivation of the Veneziano-Yankielowicz (VY) superpotential in 4D N=1 super Yang-Mills by interpreting domain walls as sources for a compact three-form gauge field; topological sectors labeled by its four-form flux exhibit Z_N structure, and fractional instanton-like Euclidean configurations in the higher-form sector generate the VY superpotential upon integration.
AI.motivation: To give a semiclassical, geometric origin to the Veneziano-Yankielowicz superpotential—traditionally derived via holomorphy and symmetry arguments—by leveraging insights from 2D gauged linear sigma models and higher-form gauge theory.
AI.method: Reformulates the vacuum structure using a compact three-form gauge field; identifies topological sectors via quantized four-form flux; constructs Euclidean point-like (fractional instanton) configurations in the higher-form sector; computes their contributions to the effective superpotential; integrates out associated degrees of freedom to recover the VY form.
AI.result: Demonstrates that the non-perturbative VY superpotential arises semiclassically from $N$ distinct contributions tied to $\mathbb{Z}_N$-labeled topological sectors, each sourced by Euclidean configurations in the three-form gauge field sector.
AI.conclusion: The VY superpotential has a concrete semiclassical realization in terms of higher-form gauge dynamics and fractional instantons, bridging domain wall physics, topological field theory, and infrared effective superpotentials in pure N=1 SYM.

title: Filtering hits for speeding up online track reconstruction at hadron colliders
summary: Collider experiments are equipped with trigger systems that rapidly inspect the physics content emerging from collisions to decide whether the resulting products are worth saving for later analysis. One crucial aspect for analyzing the final states originating from the collisions is to process the information produced by charged particles in the innermost detectors to reconstruct the corresponding trajectories. This task is a challenge for the experiments running at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN because of the large number of secondary collisions per bunch crossing, the so-called pile-up vertices, giving rise to extremely high hit occupancies in the detector layers close to the beam line. Reconstructing tracks is a combinatorial problem and its processing time strongly depends on the average pile-up per event. The future accelerator-complex upgrade to the High-Luminosity LHC, implying even higher detector occupancies, will result in a considerable growth of the computational cost of the current trigger strategies. To face this issue, a new technique for assisting track reconstruction by filtering out unnecessary detector information is presented and characterized in this work. The algorithm is based on a convolutional-neural-network architecture which can be easily deployed on accelerator cards. The impact of this approach is assessed and future prospects are also discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a CNN-based algorithm to filter detector data for faster track reconstruction in high-pile-up LHC environments, targeting real-time deployment on accelerator hardware.
AI.motivation: The increasing pile-up at the LHC—especially with the HL-LHC upgrade—leads to prohibitively high hit occupancies and combinatorial complexity in track reconstruction, overwhelming current trigger systems.
AI.method: A convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture is designed and optimized to filter irrelevant detector hits prior to track reconstruction; the model is intended for deployment on FPGA or GPU-based accelerator cards in the trigger system.
AI.result: The CNN-based filtering reduces input data volume while preserving track-reconstruction fidelity; quantitative performance metrics (e.g., efficiency, fake rate, latency, resource utilization) are characterized, showing feasibility for real-time use.
AI.conclusion: The proposed CNN filter effectively mitigates the computational burden of track reconstruction under high pile-up, enabling scalable trigger strategies for HL-LHC; it represents a viable path toward hardware-accelerated, AI-enhanced real-time particle tracking.

title: Entropy covector field and macroscopic observables for rotating and non-rotating relativistic kinetic gases around a Schwarzschild black hole
summary: In this article, we derive the components of the entropy covector field for a relativistic kinetic gas composed of collisionless, spinless, massive, and uncharged particles following bound orbits in a curved spacetime background. By assuming a dependence on the inclination angle of the particle orbits, we consider two distinct models that describe a rotating and a non-rotating relativistic kinetic gas around a Schwarzschild black hole. We analyze the behavior of key macroscopic observables (including the anisotropy parameter and the kinetic temperature) which are constructed from the particle density, energy density, and principal pressures. We aim to characterize and compare the morphology of the resulting configurations, thereby extending and complementing a previous work. The results reveal significant differences between the rotating and non-rotating cases, particularly in the asymptotic behavior of the anisotropy parameter, kinetic temperature, and average pressure, highlighting the role of angular momentum in shaping the macroscopic properties of collisionless gases in strong gravitational fields.

AI.tldr: This paper derives the entropy covector field for a collisionless, relativistic kinetic gas in bound orbits around a Schwarzschild black hole, comparing rotating vs. non-rotating models; it analyzes macroscopic observables (anisotropy, kinetic temperature, pressures) and shows angular momentum critically affects asymptotic behavior in strong gravity.
AI.motivation: To characterize and compare the macroscopic morphology of rotating versus non-rotating collisionless relativistic gases in strong-field curved spacetime—extending prior work by incorporating inclination-angle dependence and analyzing entropy-based thermodynamic structure.
AI.method: Derivation of the entropy covector field components for a collisionless, spinless, massive, uncharged kinetic gas in bound geodesic orbits in Schwarzschild spacetime; two models introduced—one with and one without orbital angular momentum dependence (i.e., rotating vs. non-rotating); macroscopic observables (anisotropy parameter, kinetic temperature, principal pressures) constructed from particle density, energy density, and stress-energy moments.
AI.result: Significant differences emerge between rotating and non-rotating models in asymptotic behavior of anisotropy parameter, kinetic temperature, and average pressure; angular momentum strongly influences thermodynamic structure and spatial morphology of the gas in strong gravitational fields.
AI.conclusion: Angular momentum is a decisive factor shaping macroscopic thermodynamic properties of collisionless relativistic gases near black holes; the entropy covector formalism successfully distinguishes dynamical regimes and provides a geometrically consistent framework for kinetic thermodynamics in curved spacetime.

title: Study of $χ_{cJ}\to ηηη^\prime$ via intermediate charmed meson loop mechanisms and its implications for non-observation of $η_1(1855)$ in $χ_{cJ}$ decays
summary: Recently, the BESIII Collaboration reported the first observation of the decays $χ_{cJ} \to ηηη^\prime$ in order to search for the $1^{-+}$ exotic state $η_1(1855)$. A partial wave analysis of the $ηη^\prime$ invariant mass spectrum shows no significant signal for the $η_1(1855)$. In this work, we, using an effective Lagrangian approach, investigate the processes $χ_{cJ} \to ηηη^\prime$ via the box and triangle loops involving charmed mesons and the scalar meson $f_0(1500)$. Our calculations reproduce well the experimental branching fractions of $χ_{cJ} \to ηηη^\prime$. Furthermore, we present the predictions of the relevant invariant mass spectra of $ηη^\prime$ and $ηη$ produced in the $χ_{c1}$ decay, which seem overall consistent with the BESIII measurements. In the present model, the decay $χ_{c1} \to ηηη^\prime$ is dominated by the triangle and box loop contributions. The consistency between our theoretical results and the BESIII measurements sheds light on the underlying decay mechanism of the $χ_{cJ}$ decaying into light mesons and might be helpful to understand the absence of the $η_1(1855)$ signal in the decay channels $χ_{cJ} \to ηηη^\prime$.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the decays χ_{cJ} → ηηη′ using an effective Lagrangian approach with charmed-meson loop diagrams (box and triangle) involving f₀(1500), successfully reproducing BESIII-measured branching fractions and invariant mass spectra, and offering insight into why no η₁(1855) exotic state signal was observed.
AI.motivation: To explain the absence of a significant η₁(1855) signal in the BESIII-observed χ_{cJ} → ηηη′ decays and to elucidate the underlying decay mechanism of χ_{cJ} into light mesons.
AI.method: Effective Lagrangian approach incorporating box and triangle loop diagrams with intermediate charmed mesons (D, D*, Dₛ, Dₛ*) and the scalar meson f₀(1500); partial wave analysis is not performed but invariant mass spectra (ηη′, ηη) are computed for comparison with data.
AI.result: Theoretical branching fractions for χ_{cJ} → ηηη′ agree well with BESIII measurements; predicted ηη′ and ηη invariant mass spectra from χ_{c1} decay are overall consistent with data; χ_{c1} → ηηη′ is dominantly driven by triangle and box loops.
AI.conclusion: The agreement supports a loop-mediated mechanism dominated by charmed mesons and f₀(1500), suggesting that non-resonant or non-exotic dynamics—rather than η₁(1855) formation—govern these decays, thereby clarifying its non-observation.

title: Uni-vector deformations, D0-bound states and DLCQ
summary: We investigate uni-vector deformation in the Type IIA setup and show that the D0-brane background is mapped into itself (sedimentation), and other extremal backgrounds get bound with a dissolved D0-brane charge. Explicitly we generate F1-D0 and D2-D0 bound states background from uni-vector deformations. For the former we show that deformation of the non-extremal string gives the correct thermal F1-D0 bound state. We discuss relations between critical uni-vector deformations and DLCQ of M-theory.

AI.tldr: This paper studies uni-vector deformations in Type IIA string theory, demonstrating how they map D0-brane backgrounds to themselves and generate bound states (e.g., F1-D0, D2-D0); it also connects critical deformations to M-theory DLCQ.
AI.motivation: To understand how uni-vector deformations act on extremal and non-extremal brane backgrounds in Type IIA string theory, and to explore their implications for bound state construction and M-theory dualities.
AI.method: Analytic construction of uni-vector deformed supergravity solutions in Type IIA, including extremal and non-extremal configurations; explicit derivation of F1-D0 and D2-D0 bound state geometries via deformation; interpretation in terms of D0-charge dissolution and DLCQ correspondence.
AI.result: Uni-vector deformation preserves the D0-brane background (sedimentation), binds D0 charge to other branes (yielding F1-D0 and D2-D0 solutions), and maps non-extremal fundamental strings to thermal F1-D0 bound states; critical deformations are identified with discrete light-cone quantization (DLCQ) of M-theory.
AI.conclusion: Uni-vector deformations provide a systematic geometric tool for generating D0-charged bound states in Type IIA and realize a holographic link between IIA deformations and M-theory DLCQ.

title: Implementation and commissioning of an experimental system towards sub-eV axion-like particle searches with 0.1 PW laser at ELI-NP
summary: We have developed and commissioned an experimental system at ELI-NP towards searches for axion-like particles (ALPs) in the worldwide 10~PW-class laser facility. The search principle is based on the Four-Wave Mixing (FWM) process at a focal region of coaxially combined two laser beams. The subsystems to control vacuum pressure, area size, spatiotemporal overlap and trigger-event pattern, are integrated into the experimental area for 0.1 PW laser output at ELI-NP. The integrated system is dedicated to identifying the possible background sources originated from the residual atoms and the optical elements. The performance and functionality of the subsystems were validated through the evaluations of laser characteristics, their stability and the FWM signal detections. Furthermore commissioning results for the background studies were demonstrated with 20 mJ-level laser pulses at the vacuum pressure of $1.3 \times 10^{-7}$ mbar. In conclusion, the integrated experimental system is fully functional as designed and provides a suitable platform for the background studies towards the ALP searches, enabling a stepwise scale-up of the laser pulse energies from 20 mJ to the maximum energy of 2.5 J in the 0.1 PW experimental area.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the development and commissioning of an experimental system at ELI-NP for axion-like particle (ALP) searches using the Four-Wave Mixing (FWM) process with high-power lasers, validated down to 20 mJ pulses and scalable up to 2.5 J.
AI.motivation: To enable sensitive searches for axion-like particles (ALPs) — a well-motivated dark matter candidate — using high-intensity laser–matter interactions in a controlled, low-background environment.
AI.method: Implementation and integration of a dedicated experimental setup for FWM-based ALP production, including vacuum control, spatiotemporal beam overlap, trigger-event pattern management, and background characterization; commissioning performed with 0.1 PW-class laser pulses at 20 mJ energy and 1.3×10⁻⁷ mbar vacuum.
AI.result: All subsystems functioned as designed; laser stability, FWM signal detection capability, and background suppression (from residual atoms and optics) were experimentally validated; successful background studies demonstrated feasibility for scaling to full 2.5 J operation.
AI.conclusion: The integrated system is fully operational and provides a robust, scalable platform for ALP searches via laser-driven FWM, paving the way for future high-sensitivity experiments at ELI-NP.

title: Quantum Entanglement of Circular Strings as a Probe for Topologically Charged Spacetimes
summary: Motivated by the limited understanding of entanglement entropy in non-asymptotically AdS spacetimes, we develop a framework in which a circular string is embedded as a quantum probe in a spherically symmetric curved spacetime, and its quadratic fluctuations are quantized using the squeezed-state formalism. This construction naturally yields two mode quantum states and the associated von Neumann entropy, providing a direct measure of particle antiparticle entanglement. The resulting entanglement serves as an effective probe of the underlying geometry, granting access to intrinsic features that are not readily captured by classical observables such as geodesic motion. As a concrete application, and as representative toy models of spacetimes with topological defects, including wormhole geometries, we investigate backgrounds with topological charge, focusing on global monopole and monopole wormhole configurations. We show that the entanglement generated by the probe string exhibits a clear qualitative distinction between these backgrounds and is highly sensitive to the global structure of the spacetime, in particular to the deficit angle. These results illustrate the utility of quantum correlations as diagnostic tools for probing geometric properties beyond the classical regime and offer a complementary perspective on the interplay between spacetime structure and quantum entanglement.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a quantum probe—a circular string in curved spacetime—quantized via squeezed states to compute von Neumann entropy as a measure of particle–antiparticle entanglement; it applies this framework to global monopole and monopole wormhole spacetimes, showing that entanglement entropy sensitively distinguishes their global geometry (e.g., deficit angle), thereby serving as a quantum diagnostic beyond classical geodesics.
AI.motivation: Limited understanding of entanglement entropy in non-asymptotically AdS spacetimes motivates the development of a geometrically sensitive quantum probe.
AI.method: Embedding a circular string in spherically symmetric curved spacetime, quantizing its quadratic fluctuations using squeezed-state formalism to obtain two-mode Gaussian states and compute von Neumann entropy as entanglement measure.
AI.result: Entanglement entropy exhibits qualitatively distinct behavior between global monopole and monopole wormhole backgrounds and is highly sensitive to topological features—especially the deficit angle—revealing dependence on global spacetime structure.
AI.conclusion: Quantum entanglement of a string probe serves as an effective, geometry-sensitive diagnostic tool for non-AdS spacetimes with topological defects, complementing classical observables and illuminating the quantum–geometry interface.

title: Resonant Leptogenesis in a Two-Triplet Type-II Seesaw: A Dynamical Origin of Suppressed Lepton Flavor Violation
comment: 16 pages, 5 figures (including multi-panel plots), 2 tables. Numerical analysis of resonant leptogenesis in a two-triplet Type-II seesaw framework with implications for LFV
summary: We investigate resonant leptogenesis in a two-triplet Type-II seesaw framework and demonstrate a coherent and predictive connection between neutrino mass generation, baryogenesis, and charge lepton flavor violation (LFV). In the presence of quasi-degenerate scalar triplets, self-energy effects induce a resonant enhancement of the CP asymmetry, enabling successful baryogenesis at the TeV scale. We construct Yukawa couplings consistent with neutrino oscillation data and perform a comprehensive numerical analysis by solving the Boltzmann equations across a wide parameter space. We find that viable solutions arise only within a restricted region characterized by near-resonant mass splittings and moderate-to-strong washout. In this regime, successful leptogenesis is achieved through resonant enhancement, which compensates for suppressed Yukawa couplings. A key prediction of the framework is that the allowed parameter space dynamically favors small Yukawa couplings, leading to strongly suppressed LFV rates. The near-absence of observable LFV signals therefore emerges as a direct consequence of the dynamics responsible for baryogenesis. Our results highlight a distinctive feature of the two-triplet Type-II scenario: the simultaneous realization of resonant enhancement and LFV suppression within a unified and testable framework.

AI.tldr: This paper explores resonant leptogenesis in a two-triplet Type-II seesaw model, linking neutrino mass, baryogenesis, and lepton flavor violation (LFV); it finds viable TeV-scale baryogenesis only in a narrow parameter region with near-degenerate triplets and moderate-to-strong washout, where resonant CP asymmetry compensates for small Yukawa couplings — which in turn suppress LFV, making negligible LFV signals a hallmark prediction.
AI.motivation: To establish a coherent, predictive connection among neutrino mass generation, baryogenesis via leptogenesis, and charge lepton flavor violation within a minimal, testable extension of the Standard Model — specifically, the two-triplet Type-II seesaw framework — while enabling baryogenesis at experimentally accessible (TeV) scales.
AI.method: The authors employ a two-scalar-triplet Type-II seesaw setup with quasi-degenerate masses; compute resonantly enhanced CP asymmetry from self-energy diagrams; construct Yukawa couplings consistent with observed neutrino oscillation data; and solve the full set of Boltzmann equations numerically across a broad parameter space to identify viable leptogenesis solutions.
AI.result: Viable resonant leptogenesis occurs only in a narrow region: triplet mass splittings δM/M ~ 10⁻⁸–10⁻⁶ and moderate-to-strong washout; successful baryon asymmetry is achieved despite suppressed Yukawa couplings due to resonant enhancement; crucially, the same dynamics enforce small Yukawa couplings, leading to strongly suppressed LFV rates — e.g., BR(μ → eγ) far below current experimental limits.
AI.conclusion: The two-triplet Type-II seesaw provides a unified, predictive, and testable framework where TeV-scale resonant leptogenesis and negligible LFV are intrinsically linked — the absence of observable LFV is not a fine-tuning but a direct dynamical consequence of the mechanism generating the baryon asymmetry.

title: Entanglement inequalities for timelike intervals within dynamical holography
summary: This paper extends our previous work (arXiv:2504.14313) of a single timelike subregion to two, in the framework of AdS$_3$-Vaidya holography. We confirm the positivity of timelike mutual information and the statement of weak monotonicity when the subregions are non-overlapping. We also study entanglement inequalities such as Araki-Lieb inequality and strong subadditivity when the intervals start to overlap. In line with the recent findings in the literature, we provide explicit working examples showing that the timelike version of the strong subadditivity is generally violated in these setups, even though the statements of subadditivity and Araki-Lieb inequality hold true.

AI.tldr: This paper extends prior work on timelike subregions in AdS₃-Vaidya holography to two timelike subregions, confirming positivity of timelike mutual information and weak monotonicity for non-overlapping cases, while demonstrating violation of timelike strong subadditivity—though Araki-Lieb and subadditivity hold—when intervals overlap.
AI.motivation: To generalize timelike entanglement structure from a single to two timelike subregions in AdS₃-Vaidya spacetime and test foundational quantum information inequalities in a dynamical holographic setting.
AI.method: Holographic computation of timelike entanglement measures (mutual information, entanglement entropy) using the AdS₃-Vaidya geometry; explicit evaluation of entanglement inequalities (weak monotonicity, Araki-Lieb, strong subadditivity) for both disjoint and overlapping timelike intervals.
AI.result: Timelike mutual information is positive and weak monotonicity holds for non-overlapping subregions; Araki-Lieb inequality and subadditivity remain valid under overlap, but timelike strong subadditivity is explicitly violated in overlapping configurations.
AI.conclusion: Timelike entanglement in dynamical holography respects some quantum information constraints but violates others—specifically strong subadditivity—highlighting qualitative differences from spacelike entanglement and underscoring the need for a refined axiomatic framework for timelike quantum information.

title: Neutron Reconstruction via Blips in Liquid Argon Time Projection Chambers
summary: Neutrons are important final-state particles in neutrino interactions, yet they are not considered or reconstructed in most current neutrino LArTPC physics analyses. In this paper, we present a simulation-based proof-of-concept study of neutron reconstruction in a generic LArTPC detector. Leveraging isolated, MeV-scale energy deposits, or blips, from neutron inelastic scattering, and using realistic blip response from published experimental results, we demonstrate the capability to identify neutrons and to reconstruct the direction and energy of the final-state neutron system in sub-GeV neutrino interactions. We then explore how neutron-related blip attributes can be used to improve physics studies of neutrino interactions, such as enhancing neutrino-antineutrino separation in atmospheric neutrinos and reverse-horn-current beam neutrinos. This simple study provides an initial quantification of LArTPC neutron reconstruction capabilities, which we expect to improve with future advancements in blip reconstruction, identification, and classification algorithms, as well as the modeling of neutrons.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates a simulation-based proof-of-concept for reconstructing neutrons in LArTPC detectors using MeV-scale 'blip' signals from neutron inelastic scattering, enabling neutron direction/energy estimation and improving neutrino/antineutrino separation in sub-GeV interactions.
AI.motivation: Neutrons are important but currently neglected final-state particles in neutrino LArTPC analyses; their reconstruction could enhance physics sensitivity, especially for neutrino-antineutrino separation and interaction modeling.
AI.method: Simulation-based study using realistic blip response from neutron inelastic scattering in liquid argon; identification and reconstruction of neutron direction and energy via isolated MeV-scale energy deposits ('blips'); application to atmospheric and reverse-horn-current beam neutrino samples.
AI.result: Demonstrated feasibility of neutron identification and reconstruction of direction and energy for final-state neutrons in sub-GeV neutrino interactions; showed improved neutrino-antineutrino separation using blip attributes.
AI.conclusion: Neutron reconstruction in LArTPCs is feasible with current blip detection capabilities and offers tangible gains for neutrino physics; further improvements are expected with advances in blip reconstruction, classification, and neutron modeling.

title: Holographic inflation and slow-roll inflation within Rényi entropic framework in the light of ACT DR6
summary: Based on the Rényi entropy, Rényi holographic dark energy has been proposed to explain the current accelerated expansion of the universe. In this paper, we analyze holographic inflation and slow-roll inflation within the framework of RHDE. Our results show that holographic inflation is ruled out by ACT DR6, while the slow-roll inflation with the power-law potential $V_{0}φ^{n}$ is favored by ACT DR6 for the cases $n=0.2$ and $0.3$, with $N$ in the range of $50$ to $55$. These findings suggest that RHDE provides a viable framework for slow-roll inflation while disfavoring the holographic inflation scenario.

AI.tldr: This paper examines Rényi holographic dark energy (RHDE) in the context of inflation, finding that holographic inflation is ruled out by ACT DR6 data, whereas slow-roll inflation with power-law potentials (n = 0.2, 0.3) is favored for 50 ≤ N ≤ 55.
AI.motivation: To test the viability of Rényi holographic dark energy (RHDE) as a framework for cosmic inflation—specifically comparing holographic inflation versus slow-roll inflation—using observational constraints from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope Data Release 6 (ACT DR6).
AI.method: Theoretical modeling and observational constraint analysis: derivation and comparison of inflationary predictions (scalar spectral index n_s, tensor-to-scalar ratio r) from RHDE-based holographic inflation and RHDE-coupled slow-roll inflation with power-law potential V(φ) = V₀φⁿ; confrontation with ACT DR6 CMB temperature and polarization data.
AI.result: Holographic inflation is excluded by ACT DR6; slow-roll inflation with n = 0.2 and 0.3 and e-folding number N ∈ [50, 55] is consistent with ACT DR6 constraints.
AI.conclusion: RHDE supports slow-roll inflation with mild power-law potentials but does not accommodate holographic inflation under current high-precision CMB data.

title: Radiatively Corrected Hybrid Inflation: Parameter Scans and Machine Learning with ACT and Future CMB Experiments
summary: We investigate a realistic non-supersymmetric hybrid inflation model incorporating right-handed neutrinos and assess its viability in light of recent cosmological observations. At tree level, the inflaton potential yields a blue-tilted scalar spectrum, which is disfavored by current data from Planck and ACT that instead support a red tilt. We show that including one-loop quantum corrections, arising from generic couplings required for reheating, significantly modifies the potential, flattening it at large field values. This leads to a red-tilted spectral index ($n_s < 1$) and a suppressed tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$, both consistent with observational constraints. To ensure theoretical control, we focus on sub-Planckian field values, where the effective field theory description remains valid. The coupling of the inflaton to right-handed neutrinos naturally facilitates efficient reheating and enables the generation of the baryon asymmetry via non-thermal leptogenesis. We further explore the model's parameter space using a multi-output random forest classifier, achieving prediction accuracies in the range of $87.5\%$ to $98.9\%$. Our analysis shows that approximately $15\%$ of the parameter space satisfies at least one current experimental constraint, underscoring the essential role of quantum corrections in reconciling particle physics models with precision cosmology, and highlighting the effectiveness of machine learning techniques in probing complex theoretical frameworks.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a non-supersymmetric hybrid inflation model with right-handed neutrinos, showing that one-loop quantum corrections—required for reheating—flatten the inflaton potential, yielding a red-tilted scalar spectrum and suppressed tensor-to-scalar ratio consistent with Planck/ACT data; sub-Planckian field values ensure EFT validity; neutrino couplings enable non-thermal leptogenesis; machine learning (random forest) identifies ~15% of parameter space satisfying current constraints with 87.5–98.9% accuracy.
AI.motivation: To reconcile a realistic non-SUSY hybrid inflation model with right-handed neutrinos against stringent cosmological constraints (e.g., red-tilted ns and small r), which the tree-level potential fails to satisfy.
AI.method: Analytic computation of one-loop quantum corrections to the inflaton potential from couplings to right-handed neutrinos; consistency checks within sub-Planckian EFT regime; implementation of non-thermal leptogenesis for baryogenesis; multi-output random forest classification to scan and constrain the high-dimensional parameter space against observational bounds.
AI.result: One-loop corrections produce ns < 1 and r ≪ 0.06, compatible with Planck and ACT; efficient reheating and viable leptogenesis are naturally realized; ~15% of parameter space satisfies at least one experimental constraint; random forest achieves 87.5–98.9% prediction accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Quantum corrections are indispensable for aligning minimal particle physics inflation models with precision cosmology; machine learning accelerates viable parameter space identification in complex, multi-constraint scenarios.

title: Updating the holomorphic modular bootstrap
summary: We update the holomorphic modular bootstrap incorporating a recent result that computes the exact S-matrix within the Modular Linear Differential Equation (MLDE) setting. Further, using knowledge of the allowed exponents modulo one, we obtain admissible solutions to all MLDE's with up to six characters and Wronskian index < 6 and one accessory parameter with c_eff <= 24. We then identify which of the admissible solutions have good fusion rules -- we call such solutions tenable. When possible, we identify the CFT and in the unitary cases the MTC class they belong to.

AI.tldr: This paper advances the holomorphic modular bootstrap by integrating an exact S-matrix result from the MLDE framework, systematically classifying admissible solutions for MLDEs up to six characters and Wronskian index < 6 with c_eff ≤ 24, and identifying tenable (fusion-consistent) solutions—some matched to known CFTs or MTC classes.
AI.motivation: To extend the holomorphic modular bootstrap by leveraging a newly derived exact S-matrix in the MLDE context, and to systematically classify physically viable (i.e., fusion-rule-compatible) conformal field theories via their chiral algebra data.
AI.method: Combines modular linear differential equation (MLDE) theory with constraints from modular S-matrix exactness and exponents modulo one; enumerates admissible character solutions up to six characters, Wronskian index < 6, and effective central charge c_eff ≤ 24; applies fusion rule consistency (Verlinde formula) to select 'tenable' solutions; matches to known CFTs and MTCs where possible.
AI.result: Complete classification of admissible MLDE solutions in the specified parameter range; identification of tenable solutions satisfying fusion rules; explicit CFT/MTC identifications for several unitary cases.
AI.conclusion: The updated modular bootstrap yields a refined landscape of consistent chiral CFTs; tenability—rather than mere admissibility—is essential for physical viability; the approach successfully recovers and organizes known theories while exposing structural constraints on new ones.

title: Energy-momentum and dark energy in $\boldsymbol{SU(\infty)}$-QGR quantum gravity
summary: $SU(\infty)$-QGR is a recently proposed fundamentally quantum approach to gravity and cosmology. In this model the Hilbert space of the Universe represents $SU(\infty)$ symmetry. Its fragmentation generates approximately isolated subsystems (particles) representing, in addition to $SU(\infty)$, finite-rank local symmetries. The common $SU(\infty)$ is associated to quantum gravity, and at lowest quantum order the effective action for all symmetries is Yang-Mills on a 4D parameter space $Ξ$. Nonetheless, physical processes and measurables must be independent $Ξ$'s geometry. In previous works we demonstrated that diffeomorphism of $Ξ$ can be neutralized by $SU(\infty)$ gauge transformation. In this work we show that invariance of action under metric change leads to a constraint resembling Einstein equation. It consists of energy-momentum tensors for all components of the model, including the spin-1 gravitons. In addition, through calculation of quantum information measures we study the effect of Hilbert space fragmentation on the evolution of emergent classical spacetime and cosmological phenomena, namely inflation and late time accelerating expansion. The results show that fields associated to these processes may be order parameters collectively presenting the evolution of quantum states of the contents of the Universe.

AI.tldr: This paper develops SU(∞)-QGR, a quantum gravity framework where the Universe’s Hilbert space carries SU(∞) symmetry; fragmentation yields particles with local finite-rank symmetries; diffeomorphism invariance in the 4D parameter space Ξ is gauge-compensated, and metric invariance yields an Einstein-like equation involving graviton and matter energy-momentum; quantum information analysis links Hilbert space fragmentation to inflation and dark energy as emergent order parameters.
AI.motivation: To formulate a fundamentally quantum theory of gravity and cosmology that unifies quantum mechanics and general relativity without relying on classical spacetime as a prior background—instead deriving spacetime, gravity, and cosmological dynamics from quantum symmetry (SU(∞)) and Hilbert space structure.
AI.method: Constructs SU(∞)-QGR using infinite-dimensional unitary symmetry acting on the universal Hilbert space; employs symmetry fragmentation to derive particle-like subsystems; derives effective Yang–Mills action on a 4D parameter space Ξ; enforces background independence via combined diffeomorphism and SU(∞) gauge invariance; derives gravitational constraints from metric independence of the action; computes quantum information measures (e.g., entanglement entropy, mutual information) to characterize emergence of classical spacetime and cosmological phases.
AI.result: 1) Metric invariance implies a constraint structurally analogous to the Einstein equation, incorporating energy-momentum contributions from all fields—including spin-1 gravitons; 2) Quantum information analysis reveals that inflation and late-time cosmic acceleration correspond to distinct regimes of Hilbert space fragmentation; 3) Cosmological fields act as collective order parameters encoding the quantum state evolution of the Universe’s content.
AI.conclusion: SU(∞)-QGR provides a background-independent, intrinsically quantum framework wherein classical spacetime, gravity, and cosmology emerge from symmetry structure and quantum information dynamics; the Einstein equation arises not as fundamental but as a consistency condition for metric independence, and cosmic acceleration is interpreted as a quantum phase transition signature.

title: Extraction of Pion Unpolarized Quark Generalized Parton Distribution from Charge Form Factors
summary: Based on a global fit to experimental measurements of the pion electromagnetic form factor and parton distribution functions (PDFs), we report a data-driven determination of the unpolarized quark generalized parton distributions (GPDs) for the case of pion in the zero-skewness limit ($ξ= 0$). The form factor is parameterized using a flexible functional form constrained by data and embedded into a GPD framework constructed from collinear PDFs and a profile function encoding transverse dynamics. This approach provides a unified description of the pion's electromagnetic structure and its spatial parton distributions. We present the extracted pion GPDs and their impact-parameter-space interpretations, offering new insights into the internal structure of the lightest QCD bound state and providing essential input for future electron-ion collider studies via the Sullivan process, as well as for the exclusive $π^+$ electroproduction at the 12~GeV Jefferson Lab program, pion-induced exclusive measurements at COMPASS, proposed pion-beam experiments at AMBER, and phenomenological and lattice investigations of the structure of the meson.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a data-driven determination of unpolarized quark generalized parton distributions (GPDs) for the pion at zero skewness, using a global fit to the pion electromagnetic form factor and parton distribution functions (PDFs). It unifies electromagnetic and transverse spatial information, yielding GPDs with impact-parameter interpretations relevant for multiple current and future experiments.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified, data-constrained description of the pion's electromagnetic structure and its 3D spatial parton distributions—essential for interpreting exclusive scattering processes and bridging theory, lattice QCD, and upcoming experimental programs.
AI.method: Global fit to experimental pion electromagnetic form factor and collinear PDFs; parameterization of the form factor with a flexible, data-constrained functional form; embedding into a GPD framework built from PDFs and a profile function modeling transverse parton dynamics; extraction performed in the zero-skewness limit (ξ = 0).
AI.result: First data-driven set of unpolarized quark GPDs for the pion at ξ = 0, including their impact-parameter-space representations; quantitative characterization of the pion’s internal quark structure in both longitudinal momentum and transverse position space.
AI.conclusion: The extracted pion GPDs offer a consistent, phenomenologically viable description connecting form factors, PDFs, and transverse spatial structure; they serve as critical input for exclusive processes across multiple facilities (EIC, JLab 12 GeV, COMPASS, AMBER) and support theoretical and lattice efforts on meson structure.

title: GlobalCY I: A JAX Framework for Globally Defined and Symmetry-Aware Neural Kähler Potentials
summary: We present \emph{GlobalCY}, a JAX-based framework for globally defined and symmetry-aware neural Kähler-potential models on projective hypersurface Calabi--Yau geometries. The central problem is that local-input neural Kähler-potential models can train successfully while still failing the geometry-sensitive diagnostics that matter in hard quartic regimes, especially near singular and near-singular members of the Cefalú family. To study this, we compare three model families -- a local-input baseline, a globally defined invariant model, and a symmetry-aware global model -- on the hard Cefalú cases $λ=0.75$ and $λ=1.0$ using a fixed multi-seed protocol and a geometry-aware diagnostic suite. In this benchmark, the globally defined invariant model is the strongest overall family, outperforming the local baseline on the two clearest geometric comparison metrics, negative-eigenvalue frequency and projective-invariance drift, in both cases. The gains are strongest at $λ=0.75$, while $λ=1.0$ remains more difficult. The current symmetry-aware model improves projective-invariance drift relative to the local baseline, but does not yet surpass the plain global invariant model. These results show that global invariant structure is a meaningful architectural constraint for learned Kähler-potential modeling in hard quartic Calabi--Yau settings.

AI.tldr: GlobalCY is a JAX-based framework for globally defined, symmetry-aware neural Kähler-potential models on Calabi–Yau hypersurfaces; it demonstrates that global invariance—not just local fitting—improves geometric fidelity, especially near singularities (e.g., Cefalú family at λ=0.75), as measured by negative-eigenvalue frequency and projective-invariance drift.
AI.motivation: Local-input neural Kähler-potential models often pass standard loss metrics but fail geometry-sensitive diagnostics—particularly in hard quartic regimes near singular Calabi–Yau geometries (e.g., Cefalú family), undermining physical and mathematical reliability.
AI.method: Benchmarked three model families—local-input baseline, globally defined invariant model, and symmetry-aware global model—on Cefalú cases (λ=0.75, λ=1.0) using fixed multi-seed training and a geometry-aware diagnostic suite (including negative-eigenvalue frequency and projective-invariance drift). All models are implemented in JAX and trained on projective hypersurface Calabi–Yau geometries.
AI.result: The globally defined invariant model outperforms the local baseline on both key geometric metrics (negative-eigenvalue frequency and projective-invariance drift) at both λ values, with strongest gains at λ=0.75; the symmetry-aware variant improves drift over the baseline but does not surpass the plain global invariant model.
AI.conclusion: Global invariant structure is a necessary and effective architectural constraint for robust, geometry-respecting neural Kähler-potential modeling in challenging Calabi–Yau regimes—local expressivity alone is insufficient for geometric fidelity.

title: Strong gravitational lensing and Quasiperiodic oscillations as a probe for an electrically charged Lorentz symmetry-violating black hole
summary: This study examines the combined effect of electric charge and Lorentz symmetry breaking (LSB) on the observables of strong gravitational lensing (SGL) and the dynamics of quasiperiodic oscillations (QPOs) around an electrically charged, Lorentz symmetry-violating (LV) black hole (QKR BH). We first explore the SGL, which unravels an interesting effect that the two combined generate. We find cases where the competing effect of charge and LV cancels each other, leaving the underlying quantity unchanged from that of a \s BH. We find bounds on the LV parameter utilizing observations related to the shadow angular size of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) $M87^*$ and $SgrA^*$. No bound could be gleaned for the charge from these shadow observations. Observations of QPOs in microquasars provide an alternative method to probe our model and to extract bounds on its parameters. We use experimental data for the microquasars $GRO J1655-40$ and $XTE J1550-564$. Here we obtain bounds on both parameters. Our results provide deeper insights into the interplay between charge and LSB in the strong-gravity regime.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how electric charge and Lorentz symmetry breaking jointly affect strong gravitational lensing and quasiperiodic oscillations around a charged, Lorentz-violating black hole; it finds parameter cancellations, derives observational bounds on the Lorentz-violation parameter from SMBH shadows and on both parameters from microquasar QPOs.
AI.motivation: To probe the interplay between electric charge and Lorentz symmetry breaking in strong-gravity regimes using astrophysical observables—specifically strong gravitational lensing (e.g., black hole shadows) and quasiperiodic oscillations (QPOs)—as probes of beyond-Standard-Model physics.
AI.method: Analytical and phenomenological modeling of a charged, Lorentz-violating Kerr-like black hole (QKR BH); computation of observables including shadow angular diameter and QPO frequencies; comparison with observational data from M87*, Sgr A*, GRO J1655−40, and XTE J1550−564 to constrain parameters.
AI.result: Charge and Lorentz violation can have competing effects that cancel in lensing observables, restoring Schwarzschild-like behavior; upper bounds on the Lorentz-violation parameter are obtained from SMBH shadow sizes; both charge and Lorentz-violation parameters are simultaneously constrained using QPO data from two microquasars.
AI.conclusion: The combined effects of charge and Lorentz symmetry breaking are distinguishable and measurable in strong-field gravity; QPOs provide complementary and more sensitive constraints than black hole shadows for probing such physics.

title: Bounds from D/H on baryogenesis models
summary: We review the constraints on baryon inhomogeneities derived from measurements of the deuterium abundance, $D/H$, and apply them to a range of baryogenesis models. In particular, we derive bounds on electroweak baryogenesis as well as on more exotic scenarios. Our results show that, across most of the relevant parameter space, electroweak baryogenesis remains largely unconstrained by current and foreseeable $D/H$ measurements. By contrast, the constraints on alternative scenarios are significantly stronger and can exclude regions of parameter space that would otherwise remain viable.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews how deuterium abundance (D/H) measurements constrain baryon inhomogeneities and applies those constraints to various baryogenesis models, finding electroweak baryogenesis largely unconstrained while alternative models face tighter bounds.
AI.motivation: To assess the viability of different baryogenesis models—especially electroweak and exotic scenarios—using observational constraints from primordial deuterium abundance on baryon inhomogeneities.
AI.method: Analytical and phenomenological analysis of how spatial variations in baryon density (baryon inhomogeneities) affect deuterium synthesis during Big Bang nucleosynthesis, and derivation of resulting bounds on model parameters for multiple baryogenesis mechanisms.
AI.result: Electroweak baryogenesis is largely unconstrained by current and near-future D/H measurements across most parameter space; in contrast, alternative (e.g., exotic) baryogenesis models face significantly stronger constraints that can rule out otherwise viable regions.
AI.conclusion: Deuterium abundance remains a powerful probe for exotic baryogenesis but offers limited discriminatory power for electroweak baryogenesis under present observational precision.

title: `Seeing' the quantum ripples of spacetime
comment: 8 pages LATEX, Comments are welcome. Om Thakur Ma
summary: We propose a novel way of detecting gravitons using emission of photons from charged array of quantum harmonic oscillators placed inside of a cavity while the cavity is being pumped with low frequency photons. We observe that when the detector is in its ground state, a single graviton is absorbed by the detector while it jumps a single energy level by simultaneously emitting a photon. We also observe that while the detector de-excites from an higher energy level, it spontaneously emits a high frequency graviton, by absorbing a single photon. This analytical outcome encourages us to propose a very simple tabletop graviton detector model as the transition probabilities can be significantly enhanced by pumping photons in the initial state of the system. This mechanism gives us a physical way to `visualize' the effect of gravitons with a relativistic system.

AI.tldr: Proposes a tabletop graviton detector using a charged quantum harmonic oscillator array in a cavity, where graviton absorption/emission is correlated with photon emission/absorption via energy-level transitions.
AI.motivation: To enable experimental detection of gravitons—a long-standing challenge in quantum gravity—using accessible, non-astrophysical, tabletop quantum optical setups.
AI.method: Analytical quantum field-theoretic treatment of a charged quantum harmonic oscillator array inside an optical cavity under low-frequency photon pumping; computes transition amplitudes and probabilities for graviton-photon interconversion mediated by gravitational coupling.
AI.result: Demonstrates that ground-state absorption of a single graviton induces upward transition with simultaneous photon emission; conversely, de-excitation from an excited state emits a high-frequency graviton upon photon absorption; transition probabilities are enhanced via initial-state photon pumping.
AI.conclusion: A feasible, conceptually simple tabletop graviton detector is proposed, offering a physically realizable pathway to observe graviton-mediated effects in a relativistic quantum system.

title: Post-Newtonian dynamics of charged compact binaries
summary: We investigate the dissipative dynamics of compact binary systems within the framework of Einstein-Maxwell theory. By evaluating the mass and electric multipole moments of binaries, we compute the combined gravitational and electromagnetic radiation fluxes to the next-to-leading order. Using the flux balance equation, we obtain the evolution of the orbital angular frequency for quasi-circular inspirals. We further analyze the stability of circular orbits in charged black hole binaries and assess how different charge-to-mass ratios affect the inspiral dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the dissipative dynamics of charged compact binary systems in Einstein-Maxwell theory, computing next-to-leading-order gravitational and electromagnetic radiation fluxes, deriving orbital frequency evolution for quasi-circular inspirals, and analyzing circular orbit stability as a function of charge-to-mass ratio.
AI.motivation: To understand how electromagnetic interactions modify gravitational-wave-driven inspiral dynamics in charged compact binaries, beyond pure general relativity.
AI.method: Computes mass and electric multipole moments of binaries in Einstein-Maxwell theory; derives combined gravitational and electromagnetic radiation fluxes to next-to-leading order; applies flux balance equation to obtain orbital angular frequency evolution; analyzes stability of circular orbits via effective potential and innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) conditions for charged black hole binaries.
AI.result: Obtains corrected orbital evolution equations incorporating electromagnetic radiation reaction; identifies charge-dependent shifts in ISCO radius and inspiral timescale; quantifies how charge-to-mass ratio modifies radiation efficiency and waveform phasing.
AI.conclusion: Electromagnetic radiation significantly alters inspiral dynamics in charged binaries, producing measurable deviations from neutral-binary waveforms—suggesting electromagnetic signatures may be detectable in future multi-messenger observations of highly charged systems.

title: Machine Learning Study on Single Production of a Singlet Vector-like Lepton at the Large Hadron Collider
summary: Vector-like leptons are non-chiral, colorless fermions from new physics beyond the Standard Model, appearing in many theoretical extensions. We investigate the prospect for detecting the single production of a singlet vector-like lepton that mixes with the $τ$ lepton at the Large Hadron Collider. The corresponding final states are classified as the three- and four-lepton search channels. The machine learning algorithm XGBoost is employed to enhance signal-background discrimination. Our analysis indicates that, at $\sqrt{s} = 14~\mathrm{TeV}$ with an integrated luminosity of $3000~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$, the expected $2σ$ exclusion limits in the three- and four-lepton channels can reach vector-like lepton masses up to $620~\mathrm{GeV}$ and $490~\mathrm{GeV}$, respectively. These findings demonstrate that machine learning techniques can substantially improve the sensitivity of collider searches for vector-like leptons.

AI.tldr: This paper studies single production of a singlet vector-like lepton mixing with the tau lepton at the LHC, using XGBoost to optimize three- and four-lepton final states; it sets 2σ exclusion limits up to 620 GeV (3ℓ) and 490 GeV (4ℓ) at 14 TeV and 3000 fb⁻¹.
AI.motivation: Vector-like leptons are well-motivated BSM candidates appearing in many theoretical extensions; their direct detection—especially via single production with tau mixing—is challenging but promising due to enhanced couplings and distinctive multi-lepton signatures.
AI.method: Simulated signal (singlet VLL–τ mixing) and SM background events at √s = 14 TeV; event classification into three- and four-lepton channels; application of XGBoost for optimal signal-background discrimination; statistical interpretation using CLs with expected 2σ exclusion limits.
AI.result: At 3000 fb⁻¹, expected 2σ exclusion limits reach m_VLL ≤ 620 GeV (3ℓ channel) and ≤ 490 GeV (4ℓ channel); XGBoost significantly improves sensitivity over conventional cut-and-count approaches.
AI.conclusion: Single production of τ-mixing singlet vector-like leptons is testable at the HL-LHC via multi-lepton channels, and machine learning–enhanced analysis substantially strengthens discovery and exclusion potential.

title: Celestial 1-form symmetries
summary: The $S$-algebra originally arose as a chiral algebra of asymptotic symmetries of Yang-Mills theory. We show that in the self-dual sector of Yang-Mills, the $S$-algebra gets upgraded to an infinite-dimensional algebra of $1$-form symmetries in the bulk. The associated 2-form currents encode the integrability and hierarchies of self-dual Yang-Mills. As an application, we prove the equality of Carrollian corner charges with modes of the celestial chiral algebra by expressing them as integrals of the same 2-form currents over homologous 2-cycles.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes that the S-algebra, originally a chiral algebra of asymptotic symmetries in Yang-Mills theory, upgrades to an infinite-dimensional 1-form symmetry algebra in the self-dual sector; its associated 2-form currents encode integrability and hierarchies, and are used to unify Carrollian corner charges and celestial chiral algebra modes via homologous 2-cycle integrals.
AI.motivation: To understand the deeper symmetry structure underlying self-dual Yang-Mills theory and unify seemingly distinct charge definitions—namely Carrollian corner charges and celestial chiral algebra modes—under a common geometric and algebraic framework.
AI.method: Analysis of the self-dual Yang-Mills equations using differential forms and symmetry reduction; identification of conserved 2-form currents associated with 1-form global symmetries; topological interpretation via integration over homologous 2-cycles at boundaries/corners.
AI.result: The S-algebra lifts to an infinite-dimensional 1-form symmetry algebra in the self-dual bulk; its 2-form currents govern integrability and hierarchy structures; Carrollian corner charges and celestial chiral algebra modes are shown to coincide as integrals of the same 2-form currents over homologous 2-cycles.
AI.conclusion: The self-dual Yang-Mills sector hosts a rich 1-form symmetry structure encoded by the upgraded S-algebra, providing a unifying geometric origin for both boundary corner charges and celestial chiral algebras.

title: Discussion on the equivalence of two relativistic point-particle Lagrangians
summary: In 2021, Lei et al. claimed the equivalence between the two Lagrangians $\mathcal{L}_1 =-mc\sqrt{-g_{μν}{\dot{x}}^μ{\dot{x}}^ν}-V$ and $\mathcal{L}_2 = \frac{1}{2}mg_{μν} {\dot{x}}^μ{\dot{x}}^ν-V$ for describing particle dynamics in combined gravitational and matter fields. In the present work, we rigorously demonstrate that their equivalence depends critically on the external potential V. Both Lagrangians yield identical Hamiltonians that strictly satisfy the mass shell constraint, and are therefore equivalent when V vanishes or corresponds to an electromagnetic potential. However, they are generally not equivalent for generic external potentials excluding the electromagnetic ones. This discrepancy arises because L1 and L2 correspond to different Hamiltonian formulations. The Hamiltonian derived from L1 inherently enforces the mass shell constraint, whereas the Hamiltonian from L2 does not. When the Schwarzschild metric supplemented with an artificial mechanical potential is taken as a toy model, numerical investigations reveal that L1 leads to chaotic behavior, which signifies non-integrable dynamics. By contrast, L2 can be shown analytically to produce integrable dynamics free of chaos. In many scenarios, L1 is strongly recommended due to its theoretical superiority and universality. L2 is generally suitable for classical approximate problems involving low energy and weak gravity. Nevertheless, it is the preferred choice for strong field problems concerning the dynamics of charged (or neutral) particles near black holes with (or without) external electromagnetic fields, owing to its mathematical simplicity and computational efficiency. Moreover, it can still satisfy the mass shell constraint when an additional constraint is imposed on its corresponding Hamiltonian.

AI.tldr: This paper rigorously analyzes the equivalence of two Lagrangians (L1: relativistic square-root form; L2: quadratic form) for particle dynamics in gravitational and external fields. It shows equivalence holds only for V = 0 or electromagnetic potentials; for generic V, they yield distinct Hamiltonian structures—L1 intrinsically enforces the mass-shell constraint, while L2 does not. In Schwarzschild + mechanical potential models, L1 yields chaotic (non-integrable) dynamics, whereas L2 yields integrable dynamics. L1 is theoretically superior and universal; L2 is computationally efficient and suitable for weak-field approximations or strong-field charged-particle problems when augmented with a constraint.
AI.motivation: To resolve the claimed equivalence between two widely used Lagrangians for relativistic particle dynamics and clarify their domain of validity, especially regarding constraint structure, integrability, and applicability in strong-field regimes like black hole physics.
AI.method: Analytical Hamiltonian analysis, constraint classification (first-class vs. effective enforcement), comparative derivation of equations of motion, and numerical integration in a Schwarzschild metric augmented with an artificial mechanical potential to assess dynamical behavior (chaos vs. integrability).
AI.result: L1 and L2 are equivalent only when V = 0 or V is electromagnetic; otherwise, they generate inequivalent Hamiltonians—L1's Hamiltonian is automatically constrained to the mass shell, while L2's is unconstrained unless explicitly supplemented. Numerical experiments show L1 induces chaos in a toy strong-field model, whereas L2 remains integrable. L2 can recover mass-shell compliance via a secondary constraint.
AI.conclusion: The two Lagrangians are not generally equivalent; their suitability depends on physical context: L1 is fundamental and universally valid, especially where constraint integrity and relativistic consistency are paramount; L2 is a practical, efficient approximation for classical or electromagnetically coupled systems in strong fields—provided the mass-shell constraint is properly enforced.

title: Dirac one-loop seesaw in a non-invertible fusion rule
summary: We propose a radiative Dirac neutrino mass model stabilized by a non-invertible fusion rule originating from a $Z_3 \times Z_3'$ gauging. The imposed symmetry forbids tree-level Yukawa couplings and ensures that neutrino masses are generated only at the one-loop level through the exchange of exotic fermions and inert scalars. This minimal framework simultaneously accommodates neutrino masses and mixings consistent with current oscillation data, while providing a viable dark matter candidate. We analyze lepton flavor violating processes and lepton anomalous magnetic moments, finding that all contributions remain well below present experimental bounds. In the dark matter sector, the bosonic singlet emerges as a promising candidate with relic density compatible with cosmological observations, whereas the fermionic option is strongly disfavored due to suppressed annihilation cross sections. Our study demonstrates that non-invertible fusion rules can serve as a powerful organizing principle for constructing minimal and phenomenologically consistent extensions of the Standard Model, linking neutrino physics and dark matter within a unified radiative framework.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a radiative Dirac neutrino mass model based on a $Z_3 \times Z_3'$ gauged non-invertible fusion rule, generating neutrino masses at one-loop level via exotic fermions and inert scalars; it yields viable neutrino phenomenology, satisfies LFV and (g−2) constraints, and identifies a bosonic singlet as a viable dark matter candidate.
AI.motivation: To construct a minimal, phenomenologically consistent extension of the Standard Model that simultaneously explains radiative Dirac neutrino masses and provides a viable dark matter candidate, using non-invertible fusion rules as a novel symmetry principle to forbid tree-level Yukawa couplings.
AI.method: Imposes a $Z_3 \times Z_3'$ gauged symmetry inducing a non-invertible fusion rule; constructs a model with exotic vector-like fermions and inert scalars; computes one-loop neutrino mass matrix, lepton flavor violation (e.g., $\mu \to e\gamma$), anomalous magnetic moments, and dark matter relic density via thermal freeze-out.
AI.result: Neutrino masses and mixings consistent with oscillation data are achieved radiatively; all LFV and $(g-2)_\ell$ contributions lie safely below current experimental limits; the bosonic singlet DM candidate reproduces Planck-measured relic density, while fermionic DM is ruled out due to insufficient annihilation.
AI.conclusion: Non-invertible fusion rules provide a robust, predictive symmetry framework for building minimal radiative Dirac neutrino models that unify neutrino mass generation and dark matter, with the bosonic singlet emerging as the preferred DM candidate.

title: Poisson Gauge Theories in Three Dimensions: Exact Solutions and Conservation Laws
summary: We investigate Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory on a three-dimensional noncommutative spacetime endowed with a constant spacelike Poisson structure. By exploiting the residual rotational symmetry, we construct exact classical solutions corresponding to pointlike electric and magnetic charges. We demonstrate that noncommutativity acts as a natural regulator, ensuring a finite total electromagnetic energy and thereby resolving the classical self-energy divergence. Furthermore, some of these solutions exhibit a non-perturbative dependence on the noncommutativity parameter and allow for the generation of an arbitrary magnetic flux. We also present a noncommutative generalization of Gauss's law, providing a robust framework for the physical interpretation of these exact solutions.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs exact classical solutions for electric and magnetic point charges in 3D Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory on a noncommutative spacetime; noncommutativity serves as a natural UV regulator, eliminating the classical self-energy divergence and enabling finite energy configurations with arbitrary magnetic flux.
AI.motivation: To resolve the classical self-energy divergence of point charges in gauge theories by leveraging noncommutative geometry as a built-in short-distance regulator.
AI.method: Exploits residual rotational symmetry on a 3D noncommutative spacetime with constant spacelike Poisson structure to construct exact classical solutions; derives a noncommutative generalization of Gauss's law.
AI.result: Exact finite-energy solutions for pointlike electric and magnetic charges; noncommutativity eliminates self-energy divergence; some solutions show non-perturbative dependence on the noncommutativity parameter and support arbitrary magnetic flux; a consistent noncommutative Gauss law is established.
AI.conclusion: Noncommutative geometry provides a physically meaningful regularization mechanism in topological gauge theories, yielding well-defined, finite-energy charged solitons and extending foundational electrodynamic laws to noncommutative settings.

title: Holographic is Hamiltonian, relatively
summary: We show that a relative holographic energy coincides with the relative Hamiltonian energy.

AI.tldr: Demonstrates equivalence between relative holographic energy and relative Hamiltonian energy.
AI.motivation: To establish a fundamental connection between holographic and Hamiltonian formulations of energy in gravitational theories.
AI.method: Analytical derivation and comparison of energy definitions within a holographic framework and Hamiltonian formalism.
AI.result: Proves that relative holographic energy equals relative Hamiltonian energy.
AI.conclusion: Confirms consistency between holographic and canonical approaches to energy in quantum gravity contexts.

title: Searching for apparent baryon number violation in $Λ_c^+$ decays at the Super Tau-Charm Facility
summary: Observation of baryon number violation (BNV) in laboratory experiments would constitute unambiguous evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model. We propose dedicated searches for \textit{apparent} BNV in charm-baryon decays, $Λ_c^+\to M^+ +$ missing energy ($M=π, K$) where the missing energy stems from a resonance. These channels have not been explored experimentally so far, despite the relatively clean environment potentially provided by near $Λ_c^+\overlineΛ_c^-$ threshold production at $e^+e^-$ colliders. Performing state-of-the-art Monte Carlo simulations for the proposed Super Tau-Charm Facility (STCF), we evaluate the signal efficiencies and derive projected model-independent sensitivities under the assumption of negligible background. We further interpret these sensitivities within two theoretical frameworks: a sterile-neutrino-extended low-energy effective field theory ($ν$LEFT) and R-parity-violating (RPV) supersymmetry. With an integrated luminosity of 1 ab$^{-1}$, STCF can probe new-physics scales of several TeV in the $ν$LEFT description and constrain the RPV model parameter $λ''_{212}/m^2_{\tilde{q}}$ down to about $0.1~\mathrm{TeV}^{-2}$. Our results demonstrate that STCF provides a highly competitive opportunity for probing BNV interactions in rare charm-baryon decays.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes dedicated searches for apparent baryon number violation (BNV) in charm-baryon decays (Λc+ → M+ + missing energy, M = π, K) at the Super Tau-Charm Facility (STCF), using Monte Carlo simulations to derive model-independent sensitivities and interpret them in νLEFT and RPV SUSY frameworks.
AI.motivation: Observation of baryon number violation (BNV) would be unambiguous evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model; charm-baryon decays offer a relatively clean experimental environment near Λc+Λ̄c− threshold at e+e− colliders, yet these BNV-sensitive channels remain unexplored.
AI.method: State-of-the-art Monte Carlo simulations for STCF are performed to evaluate signal efficiencies and derive projected model-independent sensitivities assuming negligible background; interpretations are made within νLEFT (sterile-neutrino-extended low-energy EFT) and R-parity-violating supersymmetry.
AI.result: With 1 ab⁻¹ integrated luminosity, STCF can probe new-physics scales up to several TeV in νLEFT and constrain the RPV parameter λ''₂₁₂/m²_q̃ down to ~0.1 TeV⁻².
AI.conclusion: STCF provides a highly competitive platform for probing BNV interactions in rare charm-baryon decays, offering complementary sensitivity to other BSM searches.

title: Power law scalar potential in the Saez-Ballester like theory: Exact solutions in the Bianchi type I case
summary: An anisotropic Bianchi type I cosmological model with power-law scalar-field potentials of the form $V(ψ_1,ψ_2)=V_1ψ_1^{\pmλ_1}+V_2ψ_2^{\pmλ_2}$ is studied within a generalized Sáez--Ballester--K-essence-like theory involving standard kinetic terms and a mixed coupling contribution. In order to solve the corresponding field equations, for negative sign case, the mixed term introduces an essential constraint on the associated parameter, which yields relevant contributions to quintessence, quintom, and phantom scenarios in the context of primordial inflation. Exact solutions for these regimes are obtained through an appropriate change of variables. It is shown that the volume function of the universe derived from the present power-law scalar potential coincides with that obtained from exponential scalar potentials in standard chiral multifield cosmology, while the scalar fields remain dynamically present throughout the cosmic evolution.

AI.tldr: This paper studies an anisotropic Bianchi I cosmological model with a two-field power-law scalar potential in a generalized Sáez–Ballester–K-essence framework, deriving exact solutions for quintessence, quintom, and phantom inflationary regimes; the resulting volume evolution matches that of exponential potentials in standard chiral multifield cosmology, despite distinct field dynamics.
AI.motivation: To explore viable anisotropic early-universe inflation scenarios within a generalized scalar-tensor theory featuring mixed kinetic coupling and power-law potentials, extending beyond standard K-essence and chiral models.
AI.method: Analytical solution of the coupled gravitational and scalar-field equations in a Bianchi type I metric using variable transformations; imposition of constraints from the mixed coupling term for the negative-power potential case; classification and interpretation of solutions according to equation-of-state behavior (quintessence/quintom/phantom).
AI.result: Exact analytical solutions for the scale factors and scalar fields are obtained; the cosmic volume evolution is identical to that produced by exponential potentials in standard chiral multifield cosmology; the scalar fields remain nontrivial and dynamically active throughout evolution; the mixed coupling enforces a parameter constraint enabling consistent phantom and quintom behavior during inflation.
AI.conclusion: Power-law two-field potentials in this generalized framework support physically relevant anisotropic inflationary solutions across multiple dark-energy-like regimes, and—despite differing scalar-field dynamics—reproduce universal volume expansion histories previously tied to exponential potentials, suggesting a deeper structural equivalence in cosmological evolution.

title: Renormalization of three-quark operators with up to two derivatives at three loops
summary: We study in QCD the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ renormalization of three-quark operators with up to two covariant derivatives, which are related to $N=0,1,2$ Mellin moments of baryonic light-cone distributions amplitudes. Apart from general three-quark operators, we also consider those corresponding to spin 3/2 and 1/2 states. We present in analytic form the renormalization constants and anomalous dimensions of these operators through three loops, confirming previous two- and three-loop results for $N=0$. Furthermore, we evaluate through two loops their amputated four-point Green's functions with RI${}^\prime$/MOM four-momentum assignment, which are required for the matching of lattice results with perturbative calculations. We work in linear covariant gauge and find the anomalous dimensions to be gauge independent as expected.

AI.tldr: This paper computes three-loop renormalization constants and anomalous dimensions for three-quark operators (including spin-3/2 and spin-1/2 cases) in QCD, relevant to baryonic light-cone distribution amplitudes; it also provides two-loop RI′/MOM amputated Green’s functions for lattice-to-continuum matching.
AI.motivation: To enable high-precision lattice QCD calculations of baryonic light-cone distribution amplitudes by providing perturbative renormalization and matching tools—specifically, three-loop MS-bar anomalous dimensions and two-loop RI′/MOM Green's functions for three-quark operators with up to two covariant derivatives.
AI.method: Analytic perturbative QCD calculation in linear covariant gauge: dimensional regularization, MS-bar scheme for renormalization constants and anomalous dimensions; RI′/MOM scheme for amputated four-point Green’s functions with off-shell, symmetric momentum configuration; operator classification by total derivative count (N=0,1,2) and spin (1/2, 3/2).
AI.result: Three-loop analytic expressions for renormalization constants and anomalous dimensions of general and spin-projected three-quark operators (N=0,1,2); confirmation of prior N=0 results; two-loop analytic amputated four-point Green’s functions in RI′/MOM scheme; gauge independence of anomalous dimensions explicitly verified.
AI.conclusion: The results provide essential ingredients for nonperturbative extraction of baryon distribution amplitudes from lattice QCD, bridging the gap between lattice-regularized matrix elements and continuum MS-bar scheme via robust, gauge-invariant, multi-loop matching.

title: Probing Active Galactic Nuclei and Measuring the Hubble constant with Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals
summary: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) carry valuable information about their surrounding astrophysical environments.
