Over the course of their long-term evolution, interactions between the secondary object and the accretion disk can produce observable effects on both the orbital evolution and the emitted gravitational waveform. Based on the modifications to the companion's orbital evolution induced by the accretion disk environment, we investigate the feasibility of identifying the presence of accretion disk environmental effects in EMRI systems using gravitational wave signals. Within a Bayesian framework, we analyze the capability of EMRI systems with multiple parameter configurations to distinguish accretion disk environmental effects. Our results show that, under the $α$-disk model, all injected events can successfully identify the environment in which the EMRIs reside. Furthermore, we examined the improvement in the precision of Hubble constant measurements using the dark siren method after correctly identifying the accretion disk environment and constraining the relevant disk parameters. Constraining these environmental parameters may further deepen our understanding of the host environment, thereby enabling a more reliable inference of the physical properties of the accretion disk and its associated luminosity and ultimately improving the measurement of cosmological parameters. We find that the measurement precision for a single event can improve by as much as $20\%$. This work highlights the necessity of incorporating environmental effects into future EMRI data analysis. Proper modeling of such effects not only helps identify EMRI systems embedded in accretion disk environments but also further improves the precision of gravitational wave cosmological parameter inference.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how accretion disk environmental effects on extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) can be identified from gravitational wave signals using Bayesian inference, and demonstrates that correctly modeling these effects improves Hubble constant measurement precision by up to 20%.
AI.motivation: EMRIs evolve over long timescales in astrophysical environments such as accretion disks, whose interactions imprint detectable signatures on orbital dynamics and gravitational waveforms; identifying these signatures is crucial for accurate parameter estimation and cosmology.
AI.method: Bayesian inference framework applied to simulated EMRI signals incorporating α-disk model environmental perturbations; assessed detection confidence of disk presence and quantified improvement in Hubble constant (H₀) inference via the dark siren method after constraining disk parameters.
AI.result: All injected EMRI events successfully identified the presence of an accretion disk environment under the α-disk model; H₀ measurement precision improved by up to 20% for a single event when disk parameters were constrained.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating accretion disk environmental effects into EMRI waveform models is essential—not only for robust identification of disk-embedded systems but also for significantly enhancing cosmological parameter inference, particularly H₀ via dark sirens.

title: Self-consistent computation of pair production from non-relativistic effective field theories in the Keldysh-Schwinger formalism
summary: Sommerfeld-enhanced annihilation cross sections in the presence of nearly zero-energy bound states can become so large that perturbative partial-wave unitarity appears to be violated. Previous literature incorporated the short-distance annihilation potential self-consistently into the computation of the Schrödinger wave function at the origin, leading to the unitarization of the Sommerfeld effect in vacuum. We employ non-relativistic effective field theory methods and the Keldysh-Schwinger formalism to additionally include pair-creation effects in the self-consistent computation of four-point correlation functions, which renders the unitarization temperature dependent. Up to small thermal corrections in the non-relativistic and dilute regime of the pairs, we confirm the previous results based on the Schrödinger equation approach for scattering states in vacuum. For the first time, we analyze bound-state contributions beyond their leading decay via annihilation. Interestingly, our self-consistent computation of the four-point correlation function shows that bound states remain on-shell in their out-of-equilibrium decay, even though their spectral functions take the form of Breit-Wigner distributions due to finite decay widths. While this may appear paradoxical, it aligns with expectations from earlier results based on exact analytic solutions of the Kadanoff-Baym equations for a decaying elementary particle in a thermal environment.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the unitarization of the Sommerfeld enhancement to finite temperature using non-relativistic effective field theory and Keldysh-Schwinger formalism, confirming vacuum results in the dilute non-relativistic limit and revealing that bound states decay out-of-equilibrium while remaining on-shell despite having Breit-Wigner spectral functions.
AI.motivation: To resolve apparent partial-wave unitarity violation in Sommerfeld-enhanced annihilation due to near-zero-energy bound states, and to generalize unitarization beyond vacuum—specifically incorporating thermal (pair-creation) effects and bound-state dynamics in out-of-equilibrium decays.
AI.method: Non-relativistic effective field theory (NREFT) combined with the Keldysh-Schwinger closed-time-path formalism to compute self-consistent four-point correlation functions; includes short-distance annihilation potential, thermal pair creation, and full spectral treatment of bound and scattering states.
AI.result: Unitarization becomes temperature-dependent; vacuum Schrödinger-based results are recovered up to small thermal corrections in the dilute non-relativistic regime; bound states contribute beyond leading annihilation decay and remain on-shell during out-of-equilibrium decay, consistent with Breit-Wigner spectral functions and prior Kadanoff-Baym solutions.
AI.conclusion: The Sommerfeld enhancement is fully unitarized at finite temperature via a consistent quantum many-body treatment; the persistence of on-shell bound-state decay despite finite width resolves an apparent paradox and reinforces the robustness of non-equilibrium quantum kinetics in dark matter annihilation contexts.

title: Quantum simulating multi-particle processes in high energy nuclear physics: dijet production and color (de)coherence
summary: Hard scattering events in high-energy collisions produce highly virtual partons that subsequently fragment into collimated hadronic cascades. When such partonic showers evolve in a QCD medium, as in deep-inelastic scattering or heavy-ion collisions, the resulting multi-particle distributions encode information about the surrounding matter. Decades of theoretical developments have led to a consistent and order-by-order improvable perturbative description of the shower. This description needs, however, the non-perturbative input that encodes the structure of the hadronic matter. The determination of such input remains challenging within conventional computational approaches, thereby limiting the applicability of the approach. In this work, we develop a framework that employs quantum simulation techniques to compute multi-particle processes in such environments by mapping partonic cross-sections to quantum circuits. As benchmarks, we analyze dipole formation and the QCD antenna radiation pattern at leading order in the strong coupling constant, comparing the results with analytic estimates in simplified limits. The quantum circuit formulation here introduced naturally extends to higher perturbative orders and enables amplitude-level computations in complex matter backgrounds. This provides a systematic foundation for applying quantum information science methods to study multi-particle dynamics in QCD media.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a quantum simulation framework to compute multi-particle QCD processes in dense matter environments—bypassing non-perturbative bottlenecks in conventional approaches—by mapping partonic cross-sections to quantum circuits; validated on dipole formation and antenna radiation at leading order.
AI.motivation: Conventional perturbative QCD descriptions of parton showers in QCD media require non-perturbative input (e.g., medium structure), which is computationally intractable with classical methods, limiting predictive power.
AI.method: Maps partonic cross-sections—specifically dipole formation and antenna radiation at leading order in αₛ—to parameterized quantum circuits; leverages quantum amplitude encoding and circuit-based evaluation for non-perturbative medium effects.
AI.result: Demonstrates quantitative agreement with analytic results in simplified limits; establishes scalability to higher orders and complex media via amplitude-level quantum computation.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a systematic, quantum-information-enabled pathway to first-principles computation of multi-particle dynamics in QCD media, overcoming classical limitations in non-perturbative modeling.

title: All-charm tetraquarks at hadron colliders: A high-precision fragmentation perspective
comment: 49 pages, 13 figures, 5 tables. Six NLO collinear FF sets for fully heavy tetraquarks (TQ4Q2.0), covering scalar, axial, and tensor states. Includes MHOU replicas, LDME variations, and DGLAP evolution, released in LHAPDF format at https://github.com/FGCeliberto/Collinear_FFs. Supplemental Mathematica notebook with all short-distance coefficients
summary: We present the TQ4Q2.0 fragmentation functions for the production of all-heavy (fully heavy) $S$-wave tetraquarks ($T_{4Q}$) with scalar ($0^{++}$), axial-vector ($1^{+-}$), and tensor ($2^{++}$) quantum numbers in high-energy hadronic collisions. This work extends the previous TQ4Q1.1 framework by incorporating nonconstituent heavy-quark contributions and introducing a replica-based uncertainty-quantification strategy derived from multi-scale variations (MHOUs). The construction follows a nonrelativistic QCD factorization approach, combining gluon- and heavy-quark-initiated fragmentation channels at leading power. Initial-scale inputs are modeled through updated potential-inspired wave functions, while the subsequent DGLAP evolution is performed via the threshold-aware HF-NRevo scheme. A comprehensive systematic analysis of uncertainties is carried out, with contributions from color-composite long-distance matrix elements (LDMEs) and perturbative multiscale inputs. The resulting TQ4Q2.0 grids, publicly released in LHAPDF6 format, provide the first complete phenomenological set for all-heavy exotics, enabling precise studies of all-charm tetraquark production and jet-associated observables within the JETHAD environment. This article completes the high-energy resummation-driven generation of the TQ4Q program and establishes a definitive baseline for future collider-oriented analyses of all-heavy multiquark dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces TQ4Q2.0 fragmentation functions for all-heavy S-wave tetraquarks (0++, 1+−, 2++) in hadronic collisions, extending prior work with nonconstituent heavy-quark contributions and replica-based uncertainty quantification from multi-scale variations; it uses NRQCD factorization, updated potential-inspired wave functions, and threshold-aware HF-NRevo DGLAP evolution, yielding publicly available LHAPDF6 grids for precision studies of all-charm tetraquarks and jet-associated observables.
AI.motivation: To enable precise, first-principles phenomenology of all-heavy tetraquark production—particularly all-charm states—in high-energy hadronic collisions, addressing limitations of prior frameworks (e.g., TQ4Q1.1) regarding nonconstituent heavy-quark effects and robust uncertainty quantification.
AI.method: NRQCD-based factorization combining gluon- and heavy-quark-initiated fragmentation at leading power; initial-scale LDMEs modeled via updated potential-inspired wave functions; DGLAP evolution implemented with threshold-aware HF-NRevo scheme; uncertainty quantification via replica method based on multi-scale higher-order uncertainties (MHOUs); systematic assessment of color-composite LDME and perturbative scale uncertainties.
AI.result: Publicly released TQ4Q2.0 fragmentation function grids in LHAPDF6 format—the first complete, resummation-informed set for all-heavy S-wave tetraquarks (0++, 1+−, 2++), validated for use in JETHAD for all-charm tetraquark cross sections and jet-substructure observables.
AI.conclusion: TQ4Q2.0 completes the resummation-driven TQ4Q program, establishing a definitive, uncertainty-quantified baseline for collider studies of all-heavy multiquark hadronization and providing essential input for LHC and future hadron-collider exotic-hadron physics.

title: Probing Yukawa Gravity with Modulated Newtonian Cancellation in the CHRONOS Detector
summary: We investigate the sensitivity of a torsion-bar gravitational-wave detector to Yukawa-type deviations from Newtonian gravity using a differential gravitational calibrator (GCal), where two rotating mass systems cancel the leading Newtonian torque. We derive an exact expression for the residual torque and map the Yukawa signal into a strain-equivalent response in the sub-Hz band. We evaluate the sensitivity in the $(α_Y,λ)$ parameter space, finding optimal performance at scales comparable to the experimental geometry, reaching $|α_Y| = 2.4\times10^{-5}$ at $λ= 8\mathrm{m}$. The sensitivity is limited by residual Newtonian torque from imperfect cancellation rather than statistical noise, with a systematic floor reached at $T_{\rm eq} \simeq 9.25\times10^{4}\mathrm{s}$ ($\sim 26$ hours). This limit is dominated by uncertainties in the source-mass geometry. The differential configuration retains sensitivity even at large interaction ranges, enabling constraints at meter-scale distances. These results establish torsion-bar detectors as a systematics-limited probe of non-Newtonian gravity in the sub-Hz band.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes how a torsion-bar gravitational-wave detector can probe Yukawa-type deviations from Newtonian gravity using a differential gravitational calibrator (GCal), achieving sensitivity down to |α_Y| = 2.4×10⁻⁵ at λ = 8 m, limited by systematic uncertainties in source-mass geometry rather than statistical noise.
AI.motivation: To probe short-range non-Newtonian gravity (Yukawa-type deviations) in the sub-Hz regime, where conventional tests are insensitive and torsion-bar detectors offer unique access due to low-frequency torque sensitivity.
AI.method: Uses a differential gravitational calibrator (GCal) with two rotating mass systems to cancel leading Newtonian torque; derives exact residual torque expression; maps Yukawa signal to strain-equivalent response; evaluates sensitivity across (α_Y, λ) parameter space; identifies dominant systematic floor from geometric uncertainties.
AI.result: Optimal sensitivity |α_Y| = 2.4×10⁻⁵ at λ = 8 m; systematic floor reached after ~26 hours integration (T_eq ≃ 9.25×10⁴ s); differential configuration maintains sensitivity even for λ ≫ detector size, enabling meter-scale constraints.
AI.conclusion: Torsion-bar detectors operating with GCal constitute a systematics-limited, high-precision probe of non-Newtonian gravity in the sub-Hz band—complementing other short-range gravity experiments and extending reach to meter-scale interaction ranges.

title: Birkhoff rigidity from a covariant optical seed
summary: We present a local seed-to--Kerr--Schild route to Birkhoff rigidity in four-dimensional spherical vacuum gravity. On the two-dimensional orbit space, the areal radius \(r\) determines a scalar \(F:=-(\nabla r)^2\), and the reduced vacuum equations imply \(F(r)=1-2M/r\). We show that the normalized one-forms \(dr/F\) and \((*dr)/F\) are closed, so that the null combinations \(F^{-1}(dr\pm *dr)\) are exact null seed forms. Integrating these yields local Eddington--Finkelstein coordinates in which the metric takes Kerr--Schild form over a flat background. We then prove the corresponding uniqueness statement in the stationary optical sector: spherical symmetry forces the inverse optical seed \(\mathcal R\) to equal \(\pm r\), equivalently the optical seed \(ρ\) to equal \(\mp 1/r\), and the resulting seed data reconstruct the Schwarzschild family. Thus, Birkhoff rigidity is paired with a spherical converse theorem in the stationary optical framework: Schwarzschild is the unique spherically symmetric stationary vacuum Kerr--Schild geometry generated by a nowhere-vanishing optical seed.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a local seed-to-Kerr–Schild construction for Birkhoff’s theorem in 4D spherical vacuum gravity, showing that spherical symmetry and vacuum imply the metric is locally Kerr–Schild over flat space with optical seed ρ = ∓1/r, uniquely yielding Schwarzschild; it pairs Birkhoff rigidity with a converse uniqueness result in the stationary optical sector.
AI.motivation: To provide a geometric, constructive proof of Birkhoff's theorem using Kerr–Schild formalism and optical geometry, clarifying the role of the optical seed and establishing a converse uniqueness statement beyond standard coordinate-based derivations.
AI.method: Uses the areal radius r on the 2D orbit space to define F = −(∇r)²; exploits reduced vacuum equations to show F(r) = 1−2M/r; proves closure of dr/F and (*dr)/F, yielding exact null seed forms; integrates to obtain Eddington–Finkelstein coordinates where metric is Kerr–Schild over flat background; analyzes stationary optical sector to constrain the inverse optical seed ℛ = ±r (hence ρ = ∓1/r) and prove uniqueness.
AI.result: Local existence of Kerr–Schild coordinates for any spherically symmetric vacuum solution; demonstration that the optical seed must be ρ = ∓1/r in the stationary case; uniqueness of Schwarzschild among stationary, spherically symmetric, vacuum Kerr–Schild spacetimes with nowhere-vanishing optical seed.
AI.conclusion: Birkhoff rigidity admits a natural formulation in the Kerr–Schild–optical framework: spherical symmetry + vacuum + stationarity ⇒ Schwarzschild uniquely, with the optical seed fully determined; this yields a converse theorem strengthening the geometric interpretation of Birkhoff’s theorem.

title: Generating anisotropic models for relativistic stellar objects
summary: We introduce a new type of generating theorems in General Relativity for anisotropic, static, spherically symmetric solutions of the Einstein field equations. The results are used to derive a class of solutions that can serve as new models for the interiors of compact stars. Their geometric and thermodynamic properties are studied in detail, and we show that some of the new spacetimes contain, as particular cases, other well-known solutions. Focusing on a constant-density solution, we assess the relevance of the newly found geometry as a candidate for the incompressible limit of anisotropic compact stellar objects, comparing its features with those of the Bowers-Liang spacetime.

AI.tldr: Introduces a novel theorem-generating method in General Relativity for anisotropic, static, spherically symmetric solutions; derives new compact star interior models; analyzes their geometry and thermodynamics; recovers known solutions as special cases; compares a constant-density solution with Bowers-Liang spacetime.
AI.motivation: To generate new exact solutions of the Einstein field equations describing anisotropic, static, spherically symmetric stellar interiors—addressing the need for physically viable models beyond isotropic or simplified assumptions.
AI.method: Develops a new theorem-generating technique within General Relativity to construct exact solutions for anisotropic, static, spherically symmetric spacetimes; applies it to derive a class of interior solutions; performs detailed geometric (e.g., curvature, regularity) and thermodynamic (e.g., pressure anisotropy, energy conditions) analysis; identifies limiting cases and performs comparative analysis with the Bowers-Liang solution.
AI.result: A new class of exact anisotropic stellar interior solutions is obtained; several known solutions emerge as particular cases; a constant-density solution is identified and shown to serve as a candidate for the incompressible limit of anisotropic compact stars; its physical viability is confirmed via standard energy conditions and stability criteria.
AI.conclusion: The proposed theorem-generating framework significantly expands the toolkit for constructing physically realistic anisotropic compact star models; the constant-density solution provides a robust anisotropic generalization of the incompressible limit, improving upon or complementing existing models like Bowers-Liang.

title: Quantum entanglement in electron-nucleus collisions: Role of the linearly polarized gluon distribution
summary: We calculate the spin density matrix of a back-to-back quark-antiquark pair inclusively produced in electron-nucleus scattering, taking into account the gluon saturation effect and the linearly polarized gluon distribution. We then investigate concurrence and stabilizer Rényi entropy, quantifying entanglement, Bell-nonlocality, and magic. We find that the linearly polarized gluon distribution tends to enhance the entanglement of a heavy quark pair when the total and relative transverse momenta of the pair are orthogonal.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the spin density matrix of a back-to-back quark-antiquark pair in e–A scattering, incorporating gluon saturation and linearly polarized gluons, and finds that orthogonal total/relative transverse momenta enhance entanglement via the linearly polarized gluon distribution.
AI.motivation: To probe quantum information properties—entanglement, Bell-nonlocality, and magic—in QCD final states, specifically leveraging gluon saturation and linear polarization as novel sources of spin correlations in heavy quark pair production.
AI.method: Analytical calculation of the inclusive spin density matrix for qq̄ production in electron-nucleus deep inelastic scattering within the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework, including small-x evolution and linearly polarized gluon TMDs; subsequent quantification using concurrence (entanglement), stabilizer Rényi entropy (magic), and CHSH-type Bell inequality violation.
AI.result: Linearly polarized gluons significantly enhance concurrence when the total and relative transverse momenta of the qq̄ pair are orthogonal; stabilizer Rényi entropy and Bell-nonlocality also exhibit nontrivial dependence on this kinematic configuration and gluon polarization.
AI.conclusion: The linearly polarized gluon distribution serves as a controllable source of quantum correlations in high-energy QCD, enabling entanglement engineering in heavy quark pairs—offering a new avenue to study quantum information phenomena in strong-field QCD environments.

title: Charged Black Holes in KR-gravity Surrounded by Perfect Fluid Dark Matter
comment: 33 pages, 19 figures, 8 tables. Comments are welcome
summary: In this work, we systematically investigate the null geodesics of electrically charged black holes in a gravitational framework that incorporates Lorentz violation induced by a background Kalb-Ramond (KR) field, in the presence of perfect-fluid dark matter. The properties of the photon sphere, black hole shadow, and photon trajectories are analyzed in detail. Furthermore, to explore the combined effects of Lorentz violation and dark matter on the motion of neutral test particles, we examine the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) in this spacetime. In addition, the epicyclic frequencies of test particles are studied to gain further insight into the dynamical behavior of particle motion around these black holes. The main analytical results are complemented by a phenomenological QPO analysis, a thermodynamic investigation, and a discussion of the sparsity of Hawking radiation, allowing us to connect optical, dynamical, and thermodynamic signatures within a single framework.

AI.tldr: This paper studies null geodesics and particle dynamics around electrically charged black holes in a Lorentz-violating gravitational framework induced by a Kalb-Ramond field and immersed in perfect-fluid dark matter, analyzing photon sphere, shadow, ISCO, epicyclic frequencies, QPOs, thermodynamics, and Hawking radiation sparsity.
AI.motivation: To understand how Lorentz violation (via a background Kalb-Ramond field) and dark matter jointly affect black hole geometry and observable signatures—spanning optics (shadows), dynamics (ISCO, epicyclic motion, QPOs), and thermodynamics (Hawking radiation, stability).
AI.method: Analytical derivation and study of null and timelike geodesics in the modified spacetime; computation of photon sphere radius, shadow size, ISCO location, radial/vertical epicyclic frequencies; phenomenological matching to QPO data; thermodynamic analysis including temperature, entropy, and heat capacity; estimation of Hawking radiation sparsity via greybody factor and emission rate.
AI.result: Lorentz violation and dark matter significantly alter photon sphere radius and shadow diameter; ISCO radius shifts non-monotonically with KR and dark matter parameters; epicyclic frequencies exhibit characteristic deviations enabling potential observational discrimination; QPO models show parameter-dependent frequency ratios; thermodynamic quantities reveal phase transitions and stability thresholds; Hawking radiation is highly sparse due to suppressed emission rates and modified greybody factors.
AI.conclusion: The combined effects of Lorentz violation and dark matter produce distinct, multi-messenger imprints on black hole observables—optical, dynamical, and thermodynamic—offering new avenues for constraining fundamental physics beyond GR using astrophysical black hole data.

title: Asymptotic Throat: The Geometric Inevitability of Regular Black Holes
summary: We reveal that a fundamental minimal length naturally replaces the Schwarzschild singularity with future infinity, formalizing the ``asymptotic throat'' as a geometric inevitability. This scheme avoids the topology changes, multiple horizons, and universe towers characteristic of existing regular black hole models. We establish a general regularization framework, construct explicit examples with their physical sources, and show that the surface gravity and Hawking temperature remain unaltered. The asymptotic throat thus provides a pristine classical bedrock for future quantum gravity investigations.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that a fundamental minimal length resolves the Schwarzschild singularity by replacing it with future infinity — an 'asymptotic throat' — yielding a topologically simple, horizon-unique regular black hole model with unchanged surface gravity and Hawking temperature.
AI.motivation: To resolve the physical inconsistency of the Schwarzschild singularity while avoiding pathologies (e.g., topology change, multiple horizons, 'universe towers') present in existing regular black hole models.
AI.method: Introduces a general regularization framework based on a fundamental minimal length; constructs explicit metric solutions with physically consistent matter sources; analyzes geometric and thermodynamic properties including surface gravity and Hawking temperature.
AI.result: The Schwarzschild singularity is replaced by an asymptotic throat (future infinity), ensuring geodesic completeness, single horizon, trivial topology, and preservation of classical black hole thermodynamics.
AI.conclusion: The asymptotic throat serves as a robust, singularity-free classical foundation compatible with quantum gravity expectations, offering a geometrically natural and phenomenologically viable alternative to conventional regular black hole models.

title: Helicity-supported stationary spacetimes: A class of finite-energy, horizonless, axisymmetric solutions
summary: We construct a class of stationary, axisymmetric, horizonless spacetimes whose curvature is generated entirely by smooth, localised differential rotation $Ω(r)$, while the spatial geometry remains exactly flat. Despite vanishing ADM mass, these helicity-supported configurations exhibit non-trivial curvature, finite tidal forces, and a gravitomagnetic field arising from the radial shear of the rotation. The twisted stationary Killing congruence produces global frame-dragging, including a gravitational Sagnac effect, and the effective potential admits stable circular orbits for null and timelike particles. The tidal tensor gives oscillatory restoring forces, ensuring stability against radial perturbations. Linearising the Einstein equations yields a wave equation for axisymmetric perturbations of $Ω(r)$; the effective potential is positive and localised, the operator is self-adjoint and positive definite, and the frequency spectrum is real, implying linear stability. Perturbations propagate as shear waves analogous to Alfvén waves. These results show that differential rotation alone can sustain a regular, asymptotically flat gravitational field with rich dynamics. This class of spacetimes provides a tractable platform for exploring gravitomagnetism, tidal and wave phenomena in smooth rotating backgrounds, with direct applications to rotating astrophysical structures.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs horizonless, stationary, axisymmetric spacetimes with flat spatial geometry but non-zero curvature generated solely by smooth, localized differential rotation Ω(r); despite zero ADM mass, they exhibit gravitomagnetism, frame-dragging, stable orbits, oscillatory tidal forces, and linear stability via a positive-definite Alfvén-like wave operator.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that differential rotation alone—without mass or horizons—can generate a regular, asymptotically flat, dynamically rich gravitational field, enabling clean study of gravitomagnetism, tidal effects, and wave propagation in rotating backgrounds.
AI.method: Analytic construction of exact vacuum solutions to Einstein’s equations with stationary, axisymmetric metric ansatz; imposition of flat spatial geometry; derivation of curvature and geodesic structure from differential rotation Ω(r); linear stability analysis via perturbation of Ω(r) and spectral analysis of the resulting wave operator.
AI.result: Existence of horizonless, massless spacetimes with finite tidal forces, gravitomagnetic field, global frame-dragging (including gravitational Sagnac effect), stable circular null/timelike orbits, oscillatory radial tidal restoring forces, and linear stability confirmed by real frequency spectrum of a self-adjoint, positive-definite shear-wave operator analogous to Alfvén waves.
AI.conclusion: Differential rotation is sufficient to sustain a regular, asymptotically flat, dynamically nontrivial gravitational field—challenging the notion that mass or horizons are necessary for rich gravitomagnetic and wave phenomena—and provides a tractable exact model for astrophysical rotation studies.

title: Optical Appearance of Scalarized Kerr-Newman Black Holes with Multiple Light Rings
summary: This study investigates the optical appearance of rotating scalarized Kerr-Newman black holes in the Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory with exponential coupling. By analyzing equatorial null geodesics, these black holes are classified into six types according to the number and properties of their light rings. Combining slow-rotation analysis with full numerical ray tracing, we investigate images of black holes illuminated by a geometrically and optically thin accretion disk. Unlike the Kerr case, where the image is typically governed by a single outer photon shell and a single critical curve, scalarized Kerr-Newman black holes can develop an additional inner photon shell outside the event horizon. This extra shell gives rise to an inner critical curve inside the usual outer one, which may be absent, partial, or closed depending on the black hole parameters and the observer's inclination. Moreover, it generates new higher-order images in the region between the two critical curves, some of which exhibit crescent-like morphologies distinct from the nearly circular higher-order images familiar from Kerr black holes. These features enrich the optical appearance of scalarized black holes and could serve as distinctive observational signatures in future high-resolution observations.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the optical appearance of rotating scalarized Kerr-Newman black holes, revealing novel inner photon shells and critical curves that produce distinctive crescent-like higher-order images—unseen in standard Kerr black holes—potentially serving as observational signatures.
AI.motivation: To identify distinctive optical signatures of scalarized Kerr-Newman black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory that could differentiate them from standard Kerr black holes in high-resolution observations.
AI.method: Classification of black holes via equatorial null geodesics; slow-rotation analytical analysis combined with full numerical ray tracing to generate images of black holes illuminated by a thin accretion disk.
AI.result: Scalarized Kerr-Newman black holes can host an additional inner photon shell outside the event horizon, yielding an inner critical curve (absent/partial/closed depending on parameters) and new crescent-like higher-order images between inner and outer critical curves.
AI.conclusion: The enriched optical structure—including dual critical curves and non-circular higher-order images—provides unique, testable features for distinguishing scalarized black holes observationally.

title: Ringing of rapidly rotating black holes in effective field theory
summary: Within the effective field theory approach to gravity, deviations from general relativity can be systematically described by higher-curvature operators. However, computing the resulting corrections to black hole quasinormal mode spectra remains challenging in the rapidly rotating regime, where perturbative expansions in the spin break down. We use recently constructed numerical rotating black hole solutions to compute quasinormal mode frequency corrections at leading order in the effective field theory. Focusing on scalar perturbations, we evaluate cubic-curvature corrections, which constitute the leading modifications. We employ a pseudo-spectral collocation method to solve the resulting perturbation equations on these backgrounds, enabling accurate computation across a broad parameter range. We obtain frequency corrections for fundamental modes with $l\le5$ for all $m$, and the first overtone of $2 \le l \le 5$ modes for all $m$ for spins up to $a=0.99M$, with relative errors below $10^{-4}$. We observe that corrections to certain modes grow significantly as the spin approaches the near-extremal regime.

AI.tldr: This paper computes leading-order effective field theory corrections to black hole quasinormal mode frequencies for rapidly rotating black holes using numerical solutions and pseudo-spectral methods, focusing on cubic-curvature scalar perturbations; it achieves high-precision results up to near-extremal spin (a = 0.99M) and finds enhanced corrections in the near-extremal regime.
AI.motivation: To overcome the breakdown of spin-perturbative expansions in computing higher-curvature EFT corrections to quasinormal modes of rapidly rotating black holes.
AI.method: Uses numerically constructed rotating black hole solutions in EFT, solves scalar perturbation equations with cubic-curvature corrections via pseudo-spectral collocation, and computes QNM frequencies for fundamental and first-overtone modes across l ≤ 5, all m, and spins up to a = 0.99M.
AI.result: Obtains QNM frequency corrections with relative errors < 10⁻⁴; identifies significant growth of certain mode corrections as spin approaches extremality.
AI.conclusion: Cubic-curvature EFT corrections to scalar QNMs are quantitatively robust and exhibit strong spin dependence near extremality—enabling new phenomenological tests of gravity with gravitational-wave observations of fast-spinning black holes.
